notes: Same root cause candidate as C-3.
summary: At 100% on the 50 MP Sony, the second Heal of the audit seed was refused ("Repair was not applied"), while the same two Heals work at Fit on both photos.

summary: Turning on Denoise silently re-enables bypassed Local Adjustments.
evidence: On IMG_7723.CR3 at Fit in HDR, created the audit brush and linear gradient and checked both grades were saved. Clicked the Local Adjustments eye off: compositor pixels changed and the renderer read off, but GET edit-state still read on at revision 4. Switched to Global and clicked the Denoise eye: revision advanced to 5 and the renderer read Local on again without another Local click. The shared bypass handler redraws but does not save the changed setting, then the Denoise edit reply reloads the saved Global adjustments.
felt_impact: A bypass comparison can silently stop bypassing Local Adjustments after another edit.
proposed_fix: Persist the shared Local eye change through the normal edit command path and preserve the selected state across unrelated edit replies.
check: Place a non-neutral Local mask, click the Local eye off and toggle Denoise on and off. Assert the Local eye and picture stay bypassed until explicitly re-enabled.
notes: Driver workaround 427499c0 saves the eye before Denoise probes. No app source changed.

summary: Both baseline RAWs are eligible for cleanup but the typical photo does not exercise hot-pixel repair.
evidence: Read-only production sensor helpers at ×2.3: IMG_7723.CR3 (6024×4020) had 173490 tamed and zero hot repairs; DSC00636.ARW (8660×5784) had 234541 tamed and two hot repairs. Four-phase fits succeeded on both. Both files exist under Photos/HDR Test Images.
proposed_fix: Keep typical and large, no override. ON {remove_hot_pixels:true,even_out_specks:true,speck_threshold:2.3}; OFF {remove_hot_pixels:false,even_out_specks:false,speck_threshold:2.3}. Add own #raw-even-out-specks and #raw-remove-hot-pixels clicks beside the threshold drag. Do not require a visible Fit delta for a hot-pixel-only step.
check: After blocked ON/OFF and prime, record raw_pixel_cleanup repaired/tamed, screen signature and developed-source diff; Fit visibility remains unverified.

summary: Auto lens coverage requires a known matching photo and an active distortion operation.
evidence: Read-only production _lens_modifier matched _DSC7970.ARW to Sony ILCE-7RM3 / Sigma 65mm F2 DG DN | Contemporary 020; four real coordinate rows differ with distortion OFF. Calibration includes distortion and TCA, not vignette. Historical Canon IMG_0790 match now returned no unique match in this checkout; both files are present.
proposed_fix: Override raw.lens with _DSC7970.ARW, Fit. ON {mode:'auto',distortion:true,chromatic_aberration:true,vignetting:true}; OFF {mode:'off',distortion:true,chromatic_aberration:true,vignetting:true}. Keep native distortion click plus Apply and add a Mode Off plus Apply own step if practical. Do not claim calibrated vignette coverage.
check: Assert exact resolved lens record and active coordinate correction, then compare settled screen/source signatures. Record change-to-Apply separately from Apply-to-picture.

summary: Highlight reconstruction needs a verified clipped-channel input rather than the default photo aliases.
evidence: IMG_3129.CR2 is present and the existing edge-colour-raw.js driver uses it. Read-only production opposed reconstruction at .96 found 18122/26117/1311 clipped CFA sites and changed 12458 green sites.
proposed_fix: Override raw.highlights with IMG_3129.CR2, Fit. ON {enabled:true,method:'opposed_color_v1',clipping_threshold:0.96,edge_colour_expand_percent:0.5}; OFF same fields, enabled:false. Keep native threshold and eye. Run a separate Edge colour variant on the same file (ON method edge_colour_v1, threshold .96, Expand .5; OFF bypass) if time allows, recording the GPU/CPU route.
check: Confirm clipping plus changed sensor sites and distinct settled signatures; for Edge record backend route and clipped fraction. No GPU/Electron verification in Phase 2.

summary: A RAW change made while editing SDR unexpectedly returns the viewer to HDR.
evidence: openStagedDesktopSource passes replaceSessionId and preserves the same session ID/zoom, but activateDesktopSession unconditionally sets currentView to hdr and hardcodes the initial draw, CPU fallback and Denoise recalculation to HDR. setRaw in the audit driver reapplies only zoom, so --lane sdr RAW rows may probe the wrong lane or fail.
proposed_fix: Preserve the active lane for same-session RAW re-development and pass that lane through first draw, fallback and Denoise; leave new opens at HDR. Driver should assert the requested lane after every seed/restore.
check: On a disposable RAW in SDR, toggle Highlight Reconstruction and verify the first exact frame and controls remain in SDR; repeat HDR and confirm unchanged output per lane.
notes: Patch not supplied under Phase 2 files-only instruction. Also affects raw.cleanup and raw.lens.

summary: Every lens-only re-development repeats the unchanged RAW decode, cleanup, highlight reconstruction and colour conversion.
evidence: The import job releases derived state and calls prepare_session → load_image → decode_raw, and _decode_raw always calls its inspect/decode/correct stages; the existing cleanup cache replays repairs but does not retain pre-lens developed RGB. November 22 prior equipped Sony replay attributed 10.534 s to pre-Lensfun RAW work at 78% with Micro Grain on, a different condition from audit Fit.
felt_impact: Estimate 2–4 s off a warm matched large-RAW lens Apply at Fit if it avoids AHD without adding major paging; no new whole-wait measurement. The prior 10.534 s pre-Lensfun stage is a contextual upper bound on that replay, not promised gain.
proposed_fix: Prototype a single admitted, disk-backed pre-lens checkpoint for the active source keyed by verified identity, decode versions, flags and upstream RAW settings. Preserve the original from in-place vignette; evict on source change, skip under pressure and exclude DNG special paths initially.
check: Fit own.raw.lens.distortion.click and blocked ON/OFF transition after a settled first open, comparing whole_wait_ms, phase history, byte-exact output and peak footprint; include a real Lens ON/OFF/ON repeat.

summary: Undoing an earlier cleanup edit can silently roll back a later Lens or Highlight Reconstruction change.
evidence: Only cleanup deltas append a history entry, but both forward and inverse store the entire RAW recipe. Change cleanup, then switch lens or highlights without a cleanup delta, then Undo: _execute_command_impl validates and decodes the old full recipe, not just the cleanup subset.
proposed_fix: Store and replay only the cleanup fields for cleanup-only history, preserving unrelated settings current at undo/redo; decide separately how to account for an intentional compound change.
check: Change cleanup then Lens or Highlight Reconstruction, Undo, then Redo; verify recipe and developed pixel signatures for each state.
notes: Patch not supplied under Phase 2 files-only instruction.

summary: The Highlight Reconstruction method, threshold and Expand controls can stay stale after same-session RAW replacement and overwrite the restored settings on the next edit.
evidence: The controls are populated only when the session ID changes. SessionStore.redevelop_session preserves the ID and edit-command RAW history calls renderRawImportControls on the same ID. H1 programmatic raw seed/restore uses the same replacement path, so its native slider can start from a previous DOM threshold even after the recipe assertion passes.
proposed_fix: On authoritative RAW commit/restore, synchronize all highlight fields by recipe/source revision, without resetting an in-progress draft on unrelated rerenders. Have H1 verify control values against the seeded recipe.
check: Hold the same ID, restore a different RAW highlight threshold/method with cleanup undo or a test replacement, and verify both controls and the next submitted payload.
notes: Patch not supplied under Phase 2 files-only instruction.

summary: Switching from one manual Lensfun photo to another can leave the former photo's profile selected and apply it to the latter.
evidence: Activation resets rawSettingsPanel.initialized, but initialization never sets lensProfile.value and profile loading runs only if options.length <= 1. A populated selector survives switching RAWs. applyRawImportSettings accepts any nonempty selected profile, even when reached indirectly via a cleanup or highlight change.
proposed_fix: Synchronize manual profile selection to each authoritative source activation; resolve the stored profile even if it falls outside the present search results. Keep unrelated automatic RAW controls from submitting an uncommitted lens draft.
check: Open two disposable RAWs with different saved manual profiles, then adjust cleanup on the second and assert the submitted profile and resulting lens metadata still belong to the second.
notes: Patch not supplied under Phase 2 files-only instruction.

summary: A lens-only change can repeat full-resolution Micro Grain rendering even when the earlier Bayer preparation is reusable.
evidence: preparation_key excludes lens and the November 22 kept-zoom replay reported 0.012 s reused Bayer preparation, but 23.296 s full Micro rendering and 40.307 s action-to-result. Replacement clears session Micro cache and cooked preview keys include lens. Clean Grain is downstream of corrected RGB and cannot share old pixels unless the new corrected source is byte-identical.
felt_impact: Potentially several to ~20 s off a warm large-RAW Micro-enabled lens change if the prior full pre-lens result is reusable. Prior measured repeat cost was 23.296 s of 40.307 s at 78%; default H1 Clean Grain probes would not expose it.
proposed_fix: For the enabled-Micro route, evaluate reusing one admitted scratch-backed pre-lens Micro render or safely reusable tiles keyed by Bayer prep plus controls, omitting lens only before lens processing. Keep lens-specific corrected output and do not retain ordinary Clean Grain state across real pixel changes.
check: After the standard blocked raw.lens Fit probes, run a separate warm lens Apply at Fit and retained zoom with Micro Grain enabled; compare first/exact, phase breakdown, peaks, and exact CPU/GPU output as applicable.

summary: Lensfun remap repeats the same coordinate math per channel for the no-TCA layout.
evidence: The native strip driver is already parallel and bounded. In C, for layout=2 channel_step=0 and the inner loop repeats clipping, bounds and weight calculation for identical x/y. Layout=6 can differ per channel. Historical four-pixel coordinate grid failed pixel parity and even perceptual limits on Sony (import-and-raw.md). November 22 native lens-only measurements were 0.127–0.262 s isolated and 0.618 s within the previous Sony warm 78% replay.
felt_impact: Likely <0.2 s at Fit based on documented post-native correction timings. Prioritize only if H1 measures a larger native remap share.
proposed_fix: First split layout=2 and compute weights once per pixel; if profiling justifies it, try SIMD without changing float64 operation order, NaN/edge handling or adding FMA. Keep Lensfun's exact coordinates, not a coarse grid. Do not use full-frame NumPy vectorization or add GPU for this gain.
check: Timed native own lens distortion/Apply on matched Sony at Fit, plus distortion-only layout=2 and TCA layout=6 controls; compare native stage and whole wait with exact byte parity and current lens guards.

summary: Grade writes a second full-size source after developing large RAWs into scratch memory.
evidence: On the production Grade store file_back_sources=True, empty_source_array uses anonymous mmap over 256 MiB and prepare_session subsequently spills the corrected image into a new file-backed source. At 50.09 MP float RGB is about 601 MB each; during lens remap input+output are about 1.20 GB, with ~80 MB of six-worker TCA strips and prior source pages potentially still resident. The spill is later, not additive to that lens input peak by default. Preview GPU resources have already been released; risk is physical footprint, not guaranteed residency.
felt_impact: Estimated ~0.2–1 s on a 50 MP Apply if the second write is on the critical path; ~600 MB less write traffic and transient overlap, not a claim of 600 MB lower whole-app footprint.
proposed_fix: Measure spill/readback first; where a distinct final remap output exists, investigate writing to the final admitted Grade source map in place and transferring ownership atomically. Preserve the old source for cancellation. Do not grow RAM limits.
check: Large RAW Fit own lens change and focus on source spill, memory sampler and new proxy upload; include cancelled/retried development and same-byte comparison.

summary: Opposed reconstruction materializes a float mosaic and clipping mask even on entirely unclipped photos.
evidence: The default enabled path allocates normalized float32 then white-balances it, allocates a full boolean mask, populates it and only then tests for no clipped samples. At 50.09 MP this is about 250 MB above the existing sensor, before transient comparisons. Exact clipping uses float32 black subtraction, inverse span, white balance and effective threshold in that order.
felt_impact: Likely ~0.1–0.4 s and about 250 MB less highlight scratch on large DR-safe RAWs; no gain expected on the fully clipped-path audit recipe.
proposed_fix: When Phase 3 shows no-clipped cases matter, evaluate bounded-strip detection with exact arithmetic and a no-clips return before full allocation. For sparse clips avoid blindly paying for an extra full pass; keep exact metadata and reference order.
check: Add unclipped 50 MP default-ON supplemental run, compare whole wait/footprint plus full diagnostics against the current path; use standard IMG_3129 clipped run to bound the extra cost.

summary: CPU Edge fallback has several full-size planes live together while the old Grade source is retained.
evidence: The first propagation stage can hold input RGB, clip ratio, luma, chroma, source weight, carried RGB and found coverage: 13 float channels (~2.60 GB at 50 MP) before blur/worker scratch; prior Grade source is a ~600 MB file map with variable residency. On 8 GB Neo the 4 GB whole-app ceiling can be pressured. Large intermediates allocate ordinary np.empty, though blur temporaries are downsampled or stripped. No new overrun measured.
felt_impact: Primary benefit is reducing swap/ceiling risk, not a guaranteed latency gain. Aim to remove one ~600 MB RGB temporary from the resident peak; speed gain unmeasured.
proposed_fix: Profile live memory before changing anything. If needed, spill admitted non-local planes or generate reusable luma/chroma per strip where order stays exact. Keep existing cancellation and no-clips short circuit.
check: Supplement raw.highlights own Edge change with a clipped large source under controlled CPU fallback; record a full-app footprint envelope, route and end-to-end settle.

summary: Blocked RAW probe rows settle correctly but priming hides cold Denoise preparation caused by re-development.
evidence: RAW rows use 3 samples/1 warm-up per settled ON and OFF block. setRaw waits for persisted recipe and stable zoom; prime and check await stable, whose predicate requires exact current presentation and drained work. denoiseRebuilds only counts requests while timing, so prime absorbs any first-build cost. Own steps record the controls, not block seed transitions.
proposed_fix: Keep primed impact probes unchanged. Add a separate timed first Denoise enable after each RAW Apply before priming, and log RAW Apply phase history and prep identity. Assert intended lane and refresh the draft controls after scripted seed.
check: For same-source Lens ON/OFF, compare cold first Clean Grain enable, primed re-enable, processor route and rebuild counts, then repeat with an exact no-pixel-change recipe.

summary: Apply with no changes still tears down preview and Denoise preparation and starts an entire RAW replacement.
evidence: The production Apply path never checks the normalized draft against the active recipe. It grants a source, resets the old GPU session and submits a replacement; the backend releases old development caches before decoding. In contrast H1 setRaw skips an equal recipe, so its current ON/OFF rows cannot demonstrate this case. Profile provenance fields in Auto differ between payload and persisted recipe even when no user controls changed.
felt_impact: On an unchanged Apply only, avoid virtually all of the full re-development wait (several seconds for large RAWs; historical Grade opening ranged 7.3–9.8 s to first/settled picture across different conditions). Ordinary changed settings get no gain.
proposed_fix: Before a replacement, detect exact same editable recipe only, accounting for resolved Auto provenance and revalidating source identity. Preserve active preparation and preview. For distinct recipes whose output may be equal, require an effective-stage equivalence proof before reusing anything.
check: Audit a supplemental settled Fit re-Apply with zero control changes and source unchanged, then repeat with one changed lens control and after altering source identity; record clicks to immediate exact-ready plus whether an import or Denoise build occurred.

summary: Warm cleanup repair hits still hash the full visible sensor and repack strided strips.
evidence: The cleanup LRU already caches per-CFA noise configuration, hot repair positions and threshold-specific speck repairs. source_stamp plus _sensor_digest is evaluated before every cache lookup. _sensor_digest uses ascontiguousarray on each strip, so a padded LibRaw view can copy each strip. A 50 MP sensor has ~100 MB of uint16 bytes, not an additional 100 MB resident allocation.
felt_impact: Likely under 0.2 s of warm large-RAW whole wait if avoidable; existing caching already skips the expensive fit and repair search.
proposed_fix: Only if profiling shows meaningful delay, reuse a verified decoded sensor identity from an upstream checkpoint, or use a cryptographic byte digest that preserves exactly the same bytes without repacking where memory permits. Keep the source identity guarantee.
check: Compare warm cleanup own threshold and hot toggle with cache hit/miss counters and stage timing, including edited/replaced source and padded stride exactness.

summary: RAW replacement can carry the old source's Highlight Compression peak numbers into a new image.
evidence: LoadedSession computes fresh peak values into its new adjustments, then redevelop_session replaces those adjustments with current.adjustments without resyncing. The RAW undo implementation explicitly resyncs. import_defaults derives the fields from new analysis and selected handling, and adjustments.py consumes the stored HDR peak on a non-peak-fit route when no anchor overrides it.
proposed_fix: Copy the preserved grade and resync only derived source peak fields against the developed analysis after installing the grade and before emitting the payload. Do not change the pinned compression ceiling.
check: On a clipped RAW with Highlight Compression on, switch reconstruction and compare derived fields and finished pixels with a fresh equivalent source/grade; check preview, Proof and export ceiling, including a route without an explicit peak anchor.
notes: Patch not supplied under Phase 2 files-only instruction. Stale-field trace confirmed; visual impact depends on route and scene.

summary: Repeated transient GPU preemption can retry Edge colour more than once before falling back to CPU.
evidence: reconstruct reissues the same delivery job inside a while loop for PREEMPTED_REASONS. The retry is not globally bounded by count and violates the standing one temporary retry rule; cancellation is still handled by _wait_for_result. Actual stalls under sustained contention were not reproduced.
proposed_fix: Permit at most one retry only for the allowed transient reasons, then hand off to existing CPU fallback and retain the reason in diagnostics.
check: Mock two consecutive preemptions and confirm no third GPU submit, log the fallback, and verify cancellation does not trigger CPU recompute. Qualify fallback pixels on the existing clipped-photo driver before landing.
notes: Patch not supplied under Phase 2 files-only instruction.
Lensfun/geometry can refuse GPU Micro Grain but CPU still works. Record route rather than marking that case skipped; use neutral geometry and lens off for an explicit GPU Micro control where needed.
summary: The driver times all three Denoise methods, but does not apply a recipe per method or establish that each actually changed the picture.
evidence: seed has no Denoise-specific branch and the method loop uses app defaults after resets. The single module ON/OFF screenshot signature goes through changeState, which hard-codes Clean Grain. The skip helper checks Edge colour but only enabled repairs and omits the frontend's other eligibility checks, including non-Bayer, incomplete Bayer cells and authored SDR. Explicit nonzero defaults and all three selectors are wired, but visible changes per method are not statically verified. The method loop times its own eye after enabling and dragging, so that eye measures OFF only. Cold Clean Grain can already have been primed by earlier modules in --all.
proposed_fix: On IMG_0790.CR2, seed and hash exact per-method control maps; use the same maps on IMG_7723.CR3 and DSC00636.ARW. Clean Grain: {method:'clean_grain',amount:0.90,luminance:0.85,color_noise:0.90,detail_recovery:0.35,finest_noise:0.75,fine_noise:0.70,medium_noise:0.65,coarse_noise:0.60,grain_evenness:1,color_splotches:1,clean_splotches:true,clean_fringes:true,protect_color_edges:false,splotch_size:'small'}. Simple: {method:'standard',amount:0.90,luminance:0.85,color_noise:0.90,detail_recovery:0.35,finest_noise:0.75,fine_noise:0.70,medium_noise:0.65,coarse_noise:0.60}. Micro Grain: {method:'micro_grain',micro_luminance:0.85,micro_color:0.85,micro_detail:0.35}. Start each OFF, apply just that map, then compare settled ON and OFF signatures separately before timing. Use microGrainUnavailable(current lane) for skipped rows. Add separately timed, primed ON and OFF for every eligible method, and label a cold run cold only when measured preparation is initially absent.
check: H3 and noisy-photo Fit plus large 100%: assert each eligible method changes pixels against its own OFF control, record no_op per failed method, and retain the default Clean Grain recipe for cross-module probes. Also switch Clean Grain → Simple → Micro Grain → Clean Grain without changing view, waiting for the current selected method each time, then compare with a fresh execution of each recipe.

notes: Phase 2 owns the findings file only; prepare the output-changing patch in Phase 4.
summary: At native zoom, a cached GPU Micro Grain tile can keep showing the previous slider settings.
evidence: The Micro tile cache key contains fitKey, frame size, working space and region but not microLuminance, microColor or microDetail. The hit copies final resolved pixels and returns before writeMicroGrainRegion. setDenoiseControls replaces the controls without dropping tiles; the same Micro fitKey survives live changes. The Fit reduced key does include all three sliders.
proposed_fix: Add all three Micro controls to the final RGB tile key, leaving reusable Bayer and demosaic keys unchanged.
check: Large 100% and eligible GPU Micro source: warm a visible tile, move one Micro control without panning, require a changed exact signature and match a fresh render at the new value.

notes: Phase 2 owns the findings file only; prepare the output-changing patch in Phase 4.
summary: At native zoom, GPU Clean Grain can reuse an old colour correction after settings change, even across a packed-colour to brightness-only layout change.
evidence: The bounded Clean Grain tile key uses fitKey instead of the computed fineGrainPixelControls endpoint key. The fit only includes a subset of controls (amount, luminance, recovery, fine and medium bands and whether a fit is required), not splotch reach, fringe/edge protection, colorNoise, coarse/finest bands or the actual grainEvenness value. An existing denoiseTile hit only checks width and height, so it can return pixels from the old settings or an incompatible rgba32uint versus rgba16float endpoint texture. Fit's reducedGrainKey already uses endpoint controls.
proposed_fix: Include fineGrainPixelControls(controls,true) and the packed layout in bounded Clean Grain tile identity; keep blend-only Color Splotches (and evenness only where truly represented by the endpoints) out of the key.
check: At 100% with GPU Clean Grain, warm the same tile and switch Small to Large, toggle edge/fringe protection and edit Color Noise. Exact pixels must track the selected controls and equal a fresh render; also cover packed to unpacked.

felt_impact: Potentially seconds to tens of seconds of whole wait when a 100% toggle falls off the viewport path; near zero on an existing whole-source hit. Audit cold.denoise.micro_grain.toggle_on and own.denoise.micro_grain.eye at large 100%, lens Auto applied versus Off, then a separate CPU spatial/HDR-ceiling repro.
notes: Full-photo render is required in some cases by design. Do not claim the 25 s is fully avoidable or count previously documented costs as a new regression.
summary: Lens-corrected Micro Grain can turn a native-zoom toggle into a whole-photo CPU job.
evidence: prepare_micro returns 422 when Lensfun actually applied; non-neutral geometry also refuses the GPU. The CPU viewport path rejects spatial grade, resampled geometry or a live highlight ceiling, then main._micro_preview_raw falls through to the whole native Micro render and reduction. A 50 MP RGB float32 render is about 600 MB alongside the existing developed RGB, about 100 MB of Bayer samples, tile workspaces and possibly a disk-backed lens output. The historical Mac 78% Lensfun run spent about 25 s of 53–55 s in Micro rendering alone. The cached CPU source is independent of exposure/contrast/film, so only a cache miss incurs the native build.
proposed_fix: First isolate which refusal dominates. For an already-eligible viewport keep and reuse its exact native tiles/source across eye changes. For full-frame-only cases, investigate an exact bounded reduction from tiles rather than materializing a second native RGB frame; do not remove whole-frame guarantees or start a lens GPU port from this audit.
check: Mac 8 GB, report route, micro_render_ms and whole wait with footprint on large RAW. Compare the exact finished picture to the existing route before taking a change.

felt_impact: Zero on a cache hit, potentially several seconds on a large cache miss. Audit probe.denoise.toggle_on with Film and Detail ON/OFF at large Fit; compare grain_reduced_cache hit/miss, resize time and eviction reasons, not just denoiseRebuilds.
summary: Warm Clean Grain can lose its expensive exact Fit picture during the Off half of an A/B toggle.
evidence: Off retains the selector and its fit but turns selected to original. Memory reclaim only identifies the matching reduced Grain texture as active when selected is resolved. A normal inactive entry is eligible for reclamation, as are older entries under pressure. A miss in ensureFineGrainReduced reruns native fetch, Denoise passes and resize in strips even with a fit-cache hit and zero selector rebuilds. The eye keeps the outgoing picture until the exact result. The entry is 16 bytes per Fit pixel; at a 4096×2731 Fit tier that is about 179 MB retained.
proposed_fix: If re-audit attributes slow warm toggles to this, prefer one matching exact reduced picture over older entries during ordinary eye-Off reuse while retaining existing pressure and admission limits.
check: Prime large Fit, toggle off, apply controlled pressure and toggle back on. Verify cache retention when affordable, original exact picture, and intact safety eviction at higher pressure.

felt_impact: Zero after preparation has settled. On a real overlap, the gain is up to the already spent attempt, from a model round trip to seconds of large fit work. Audit cold.denoise.clean_grain.toggle_on at large Fit with a separate controlled overlapping probe.tone.exposure / probe.tone.contrast commit; standard Phase 3 serial priming will not reproduce it on its own.
summary: A downstream Grade edit can restart preparation already in flight even though it does not invalidate settled preparation.
evidence: The settled selector and fit keys depend on source, rendition, tier, geometry, repair generation and Denoise inputs, not Tone, Film or Detail. However recalculateDenoiseAnalysis restarts whenever editRevision changes, and the model GET/POST transport checks that same global edit revision. A Tone drag acknowledgement can discard strip work or reject a model publication even when backend source_identity and geometry are unchanged. JS measurement acquire keys the full URL including the revision and does not stop a measurement that has already entered measure until it finishes.
proposed_fix: Give Denoise preparation an input-specific ownership token covering source epoch, repair generation, rendition, geometry, scale, Denoise controls and refresh; preserve final presentation's latest-grade check.
check: Commit Exposure, Contrast, Detail or Film mid-fit and assert one preparation completes and the latest grade displays. Repeat with a real source/geometry change and require cancellation.

felt_impact: Likely tens of milliseconds on cache-hit large Fit edits and warm toggles, plus lower allocation churn and pressure when they coincide. Audit probe.tone.exposure, probe.tone.contrast and probe.denoise.toggle_on with Denoise ON at large Fit, and log blend dispatch and peak bytes.
summary: A hit on exact Clean Grain at Fit still allocates and computes a full blend texture on every draw, including unrelated Grade updates.
evidence: ensureFineGrainReduced retains packed endpoints but renderTo always calls blendReducedCleanGrain while Color Splotches is unchanged, with a fresh rgba16float output and separate queue submission; the render finally destroys the blend. A 4096×2731 Fit tier allocates about 89 MB per draw just for this output, in addition to the approximately 179 MB endpoints. At 50 MP one full-frame RGBA16F or float32 RGB image would be 400 MB or 600 MB respectively; do not assume those are allocated on the bounded Fit path.
proposed_fix: Reuse one blended source keyed on endpoint texture identity and strength under the existing allocator, evicting it before endpoints, or consume the same quantized blend directly where supported. Measure retained memory versus churn before choosing.
check: Hit the same Fit endpoints and strength across repeated Exposure/Contrast edits and eye cycles. Require identical pixels, zero repeated blend dispatches on the warm route, and no budget regression.

felt_impact: Expected tens to low hundreds of milliseconds for a first warm large Simple 100% toggle if the visible tiles are admitted; smaller when CPU-prepared packed tiles already hit. Audit own.denoise.standard.eye plus a dedicated warm toggle-on sample at large 100%; inspect actual tile hits/resolves.
summary: The first settled native render of a Simple or CPU-backed Denoise state deliberately leaves nothing in the resolved tile cache.
evidence: denoiseTilePrefix is null on the first non-endpoint, non-Micro state, so denoiseInto reconstructs even on the second render: only then can it populate the cache. The guard avoids filling tiles for every transient slider step but also excludes an exact settled or priming pass. Separate CPU-prepared packed tiles may already be retained; the repeated work is the resolved-frame tile copy/blend, not necessarily the CPU wavelet.
proposed_fix: Let an exact settled render seed only admitted visible tiles, while keeping the second-pass guard for transient, measurement and noise-view renders.
check: First exact ON, then OFF, then ON at same native viewport and settings. Check tile resolves drop and resulting pixels are identical.

felt_impact: Likely tens of milliseconds on ordinary cold GPU measurement; potentially more if removing 16 MiB of live demand prevents a measured CPU fallback. Audit cold.denoise.standard.toggle_on and cold.denoise.clean_grain.toggle_on on the first large/noisy source, logging noise_measurement_cpu_fallback and measured allocation.
summary: Cold GPU noise measurement keeps a full input buffer after its only dispatch and uses a separate command submission for each pass.
evidence: The full window set is 16×256×256 RGBA float32, or 16 MiB per buffer. The memory gate requires about 136 MiB for eight full buffers plus overhead and can send measurement to the CPU when Grade headroom is narrow. input is only used by the first conversion and could back an equivalently sized later scratch role. dispatch constructs and submits its own encoder even between GPU-only dependencies; host readbacks are the actual batch boundaries.
proposed_fix: Reuse input storage as a later non-overlapping scratch buffer and batch GPU-only chains between mapped reads in submission order. Do not change sample windows, reductions, measurement identities or policy budgets.
check: Compare complete measurement model values and rendered pixels to the current GPU path, instrument submission count and memory at the 1 MP window cap. Measurement is shared with export/Proof.

notes: Changing route changes the visible status and can change pixels within tolerance, so ask Steve in Phase 4. No patch written in read-only Phase 2.
summary: Micro Grain stays latched to the CPU after undoing the geometry that made the GPU route unsupported.
evidence: The geometry refusal in analyzeAdaptiveDenoise is permanent and keyed on the rejected geometry. runtime.microBackup keeps that old key; both renderGpuDraftInner and recalculateDenoiseForView test canRun on the old latch before computing a key for the now-neutral geometry. Ordinary geometry/Undo does not clear this backup, and loadDenoiseDocument preserves it within the same session/method. Selecting a different method clears it.
proposed_fix: Before enforcing the Micro backup, compare its source eligibility identity against the current source/geometry/repair identity and clear stale failure ownership. Preserve the latch for the same inputs and for a genuinely unavailable GPU.
check: Eligible GPU Micro with lens off, add a crop, let CPU settle, undo the crop. Expect GPU again without a method switch and check preview agreement.

summary: The audit can mislabel warm Denoise rebuilds and can time out on an accepted reduced CPU fallback.
evidence: analysisCalls increments before cache lookups, so a setup call with a fit hit counts as a rebuild. Conversely, an expensive exact Fit reduction miss or Bounded CPU source miss can happen without analysisCalls changing. The POST filter later only counts analysis/prepare URL strings, not denoise-measurement, denoise-grain or CPU preview requests, and the Tone probes do not accumulate rebuilds. stable also requires the exact requested processing edge, excluding a legitimate bounded CPU result at 4096 if the native request was larger.
proposed_fix: Count selector setup, fit misses, exact reduced misses and CPU preparation misses separately, including Tone probes while Denoise is on. Track an explicitly accepted reduced fallback with actual edge and reason as a separate route/sample, not a successful full-resolution timing.
check: Force one cache hit, one reduced miss and one reduced CPU route in the harness calibration; verify the counters, route, exactness and recorded dimensions match the action.

felt_impact: One settings round trip (likely tens of milliseconds when idle, longer behind a queued edit), zero gain if rendering needs a synchronized backend source request. Audit probe.denoise.toggle_on versus toggle_off with Tone or Film ON at typical Fit and log click-to-save-ack versus save-ack-to-first-render separately.
summary: Warm toggle-on waits for the settings save before it looks for a ready GPU result.
evidence: Toggle-off starts its exact GPU draw alongside persistDenoiseSettings; toggle-on waits for the serialized edit command to complete before checking selector identity, then starts the exact draw. If another Grade commit is queued, the click inherits that wait even on a full prepared cache hit.
proposed_fix: If the save wait is material, test overlapping only a GPU draw whose exact source and preparation are already resident, keeping owner/generation checks and requiring a successful save for final acceptance. Keep the save-first path where backend assets must be fetched.
check: An unchanged warm Fit pair should retain identical frames. Then force a delayed or failed edit acknowledgement and verify no wrong-lane, superseded or unsaved frame is accepted.

summary: Keep the visibly non-neutral Tone recipe and its existing self-reference rule.
evidence: +0.55 EV changes linear gain to about 1.46 and +0.18 contrast changes the tonal slope; the Tone eye bypasses both. The OFF Exposure and Contrast probes are already explicitly skipped at line 851; both Denoise probes still run.
proposed_fix: Keep Exposure +0.55 EV and Contrast +0.18 on IMG_7723.CR3 and DSC00636.ARW; keep the skips unchanged.
check: Phase 3 Tone ON/OFF pixel signature and both Denoise probe pairs; only ON has timed Tone impacts.

summary: Keep an explicitly authored 0 EV Exposure Band and select it before the own probe.
evidence: Default positions are [-6,-3,0,3,6]. seed clones the nodes and adds +0.8 EV to the midpoint. This yields about 1.74x gain at the authored band and a nonzero correction in neighboring tones. Selection defaults to index 2 but lives in shared UI state; ownControls already remaps to the SDR slider when requested.
proposed_fix: Keep node pairs [[-6,0],[-3,0],[0,0.80],[3,0],[6,0]] as [input_ev,adjustment_ev] on IMG_7723.CR3 and DSC00636.ARW; use default smoothing 0.5 and explicitly select index 2 before own timing.
check: Compare ON/OFF signatures and assert the 0 EV band changed during the own slider drag.

summary: The luma seed bends the curve, but the own probe guesses the handle location without using the plot insets.
evidence: An authored mid-node at [0.5,0.58] bends the normalized luma mapping. canvasDrag clicks at 42% of the full canvas height; curveEditorLayout uses top=14 and bottom=34, so the pointer can miss the handle or hit another part of the curve.
proposed_fix: Keep luma [[0,0],[0.25,0.19],[0.5,0.58],[0.75,0.83],[1,1]] on IMG_7723.CR3 and DSC00636.ARW; use the editor's logical plot transform on [0.5,0.58] for the drag start.
check: Check ON/OFF signatures and assert an actual change to the seeded mid-point on own.curves.curve.drag.

summary: The Highlight Compression seed raises peak levels but the harness does not check that the cap was exercised.
evidence: Exposure +3 EV multiplies input by eight and the eye leaves Exposure alone, so 600 nits requires more than 75 nits before the boost if the rest of the pipeline is neutral. A compositor hash can differ from shoulder changes alone and does not verify that the bypassed image exceeded target.
proposed_fix: Use IMG_7723.CR3 and DSC00636.ARW with Exposure +3 EV in both states, Peak Fit / maximum, HDR target 600 nits and Start 200 nits (on the native 25-nit grid). For explicit SDR runs use Peak Fit / maximum and Start 55%. Confirm HDR OFF pre-limiter BT.2020 channel peak >600 nits and ON maximum finished BT.2020 channel <=600 nits before accepting the row.
check: Phase 3 Highlight Compression eye/impact signatures plus pre-limiter HDR peak and exact finished ceiling checks.

summary: Every native Tone input redraws both highlight graphs and runs unrelated global panel bookkeeping before scheduling a frame.
evidence: app-boot.js input listener calls commitAdjustmentValue synchronously. renderControlState walks all rows and groups, calls HSL and Film UI renderers, and renders both highlight plots with 161 curve samples apiece; only GPU rendering is coalesced.
felt_impact: Unmeasured estimate: roughly 5–20 ms of whole first feedback at Fit under dense events, or one missed frame; settle likely little changed.
proposed_fix: Keep slider value/readout synchronous; batch dependent graph and badge updates once per animation frame, flush final values on release, and leave preview invalidation semantics unchanged.
check: Audit own Tone Exposure/Contrast and all impact Tone probes; sample time in input handlers and compare first feedback and settle.

summary: Direct SDR Peak Fit brackets a GPU-to-CPU peak readback around each eligible frame, including live draws when liveMode is set.
evidence: finishedSdrAnchor requires direct SDR and Peak Fit with an automatic anchor; settled frames qualify even with a canonical cache entry. renderToFrame submits the graph, reduces the entire finish texture into a frame-serial cache entry, awaits mapAsync, deletes the entry, then resumes presentation. Interactive frames only take this route when frameAnchor or liveMode is active.
felt_impact: Unmeasured estimate for an eligible cache hit: roughly 10–40 ms Fit or 30–100 ms at larger Direct sizes out of the whole feedback/settle wait; no expected gain for normal HDR drag.
proposed_fix: First measure the eligible route. Reuse an identical finished-signal peak where graph inputs, route/mip and signal selection match; otherwise keep first feedback independent only if the existing interactive image contract is preserved.
check: Run --lane sdr Highlight Compression and Tone impact probes, log liveMode, frameAnchor, execution mode and mapAsync timing; compare first feedback/settle and validate SDR parity.
notes: liveMode is set by the Library renderer; Grade typically takes this path for settled not interactive Direct SDR frames.

summary: A warm reduced Clean Grain delta can still be blended up front on every Tone frame.
evidence: The reduction key does not include Tone; when ensureFineGrainReduced returns cleanGrainDelta, renderToFrame allocates and submits another Fit blend before the grade, then retires it in finally, even when only Exposure or Contrast changed.
felt_impact: Unmeasured estimate: roughly 5–25 ms of whole Fit first feedback with a qualifying warm Clean Grain setup; otherwise zero.
proposed_fix: Retain one allocator-budgeted resolved blend keyed by the reduced texture identity plus colorSplotches strength; invalidate on source/mip/control change.
check: Compare tone.exposure and tone.contrast in a supplemental warm Clean Grain ON repeat; H1's isolated slide and Denoise toggle steps alone do not test this combined state. Count Fit blend dispatches and compare GPU-fenced first feedback.

summary: Moving an already-active global curve can reuse Detail's sharpen bands from the previous curve on the tiled route.
evidence: detailBandIdentity hashes serialized parameter slots and proxy identity. Curve point values live in a separate LUT buffer; moving a point with the same enabled-channel bits does not alter this key. encodeTiledGeneration runs the new base shader, then reuses packed Detail bands from the old base when packed.hit and halo assembly succeed.
proposed_fix: Key packed global Detail bands by the effective global curve points/LUT identity as well as the upstream params; preserve reuse when the curve is unchanged.
check: At 100% force Tiled, enable global Sharpen/Texture, prime an active luma curve, move its existing point, and compare to the same grade after a cold tile-cache reset and CPU within tolerance.
notes: Phase 2 findings-only; no patch produced.

summary: A Highlight Compression Start drag reruns the upstream picture graph and invalidates Peak Fit measurements even though Start is applied at the output.
evidence: Direct render unconditionally draws base through Detail/locals/Film before final composite; Tiled also emits the base graph. highlightAnchorRequest hashes the whole lane, including Start and shoulder-only settings. On a cache miss the HDR scheduler may render native analysis patches and redraw after release. HDR Target itself is not always tail-only because global Tone Whites uses it.
felt_impact: Unmeasured estimate at Fit: tens of milliseconds (roughly 15–60 ms) of first feedback if finishing alone can run; can also remove one background native anchor pass and redraw from settle/drain on unchanged input.
proposed_fix: Measure first; start with the Start slider and other proven tail-only controls. Reuse the pre-limiter finish texture and a peak key derived only from upstream inputs and selected signal, scoped to source/route/mip/current viewport and budget. Keep Tone-coupled targets in the upstream key when required.
check: Phase 3 own Highlight Compression Start drag with peak dispatch/count and all three clocks; supplement with Film/Detail enabled, and compare settled pixels/ceiling on both render routes.

summary: Exposure Bands reconstructs the same interpolation data up to 180 times per slider input and refreshes unrelated controls.
evidence: Each graph sample calls sampleToneEqualizerAdjustment, which normalizes and sorts the nodes again and recreates targets, widths, deltas and slopes. setToneEqualizerBand also calls syncControlsFromState on every input and drawToneEqualizerEditor syncs the band controls again.
felt_impact: Unmeasured estimate of roughly 3–15 ms of whole first feedback under dense input, most likely noticeable with many bands or if the old handler misses one frame.
proposed_fix: Prepare interpolation coefficients once per graph redraw and coalesce the graph and dependent control refresh to one frame, keeping the final slider state synchronous.
check: Phase 3 own.bands band-value drag plus a 16-node supplemental case; compare input-handler CPU time and whole first feedback and check rendered curve samples are identical.

summary: Unchanged global samples are already cached, but any authored local curve forces fresh packed allocation and LUT upload on every render.
evidence: buildCurves memoizes channel samples and the packed global array. uploadParamsAndCurves concatenates all non-neutral local curves into a new Float32Array and Map, which defeats its own reference-equality upload skip. Separately curve-editor.js renders and resamples the 96-point graph synchronously on each pointermove, while the preview LUT itself is sampled on rendered frames.
felt_impact: Unmeasured estimate: typically 1–5 ms of whole first feedback, potentially more with many curved locals; no global LUT resampling gain on a Tone drag with unchanged curves.
proposed_fix: Cache packed local/global storage and offsets by ordered IDs and sample identities. Repaint the graph at most once per frame with a final flush, retaining the existing per-channel sampler.
check: Phase 3 own.curves curve drag with input events versus graph redraws; supplement Tone Exposure drag with several curved locals, count uploads and compare first feedback.

summary: The default Peak Fit preset schedules an own-control drag on the hidden Softness slider, which can stop the module before its impact probes.
evidence: RANGE schedules both Start and Softness. Default mode is Peak Fit, and app code hides Softness unless mode is soft_ceiling. reveal expands collapsible ancestors but cannot clear the mode-specific hidden attribute, and a failed sample is rethrown at line 769. The generic Start drag also moves by 18% of the full 100–4000 nit range, which can cross the 600-nit target and move it indirectly.
proposed_fix: Use Peak Fit Start and Detail (not Softness) for this recipe, with a bounded HDR Start gesture such as 200 to 300 nits so Target stays at 600. If Softness needs timing, use a separately identified Soft Ceiling recipe.
check: Run a one-sample Highlight Compression calibration and check both own controls, eye and impact rows finish with HDR target unchanged during the own Start probe.

summary: The normal HDR Maximum anchor path can grow its peak cache without the 32-entry limit used by the compute path.
evidence: Bounded maximum analysis writes peakReductionCache directly at 1688 and the non-patch tiled path also writes directly at 2816. Only runPeakReduction caps that map at 32 (9923–9924). Maximum HDR is the default and does not need the compute path. Keys contain serialized lane and local recipes, so a long session with many settled edits retains old strings until session reset.
proposed_fix: Centralize all entries behind the same bounded insertion helper and retain the existing key/measurement semantics.
check: Use a lightweight cache test for more than 32 distinct Maximum keys, verify latest entries are retained and session reset still clears the cache.

summary: CPU and WGSL take different color paths for signed HDR pixels in a frame whose delivery channels are already below target.
evidence: CPU takes a frame-level all-below shortcut and clamps negative ACEScg channels. WGSL always converts to BT.2020, clamps every BT.2020 channel then round-trips. These operations are not equivalent on signed colors, even without highlight overshoot. The CPU and GPU both separately enforce the ceiling.
proposed_fix: First check signed, saturated low-brightness colors against the existing perceptual tolerances; if outside, align handling without changing the exact ceiling or weakening any limit.
check: Add a signed RAW or synthetic saturated sub-target fixture to existing HDR CPU/GPU agreement, test a just-over-target companion and use exact finished and existing encoded ceiling checks.
notes: Branch difference is confirmed statically; no observed perceptual tolerance failure or ceiling breach. Phase 2 findings-only; no patch produced.

summary: The direct Global HSL mask cache can keep old coverage after an upstream Whites edit.
evidence: The key drops FILM_RESPONSE_ENABLED..GRAIN_SEED_LOW, which also contains WHITES, TONE_LIMITER, TONE_KNEE, TONE_GREY and TONE_PEAK. toneZonesWgsl reads these before applyHsl. With an unchanged source and HSL recipe, encodeHslSelection therefore reuses old coverage if only omitted slots change. Local GPU hue leaves use the same identity. A Node-only run of the checked-in key function with the actual parameter indices confirmed that Whites 0 → +0.5 leaves the key unchanged while Exposure changes it.
proposed_fix: Replace exclusion ranges with explicit upstream dependencies shared by Global HSL and Local hue selection. Do not change selection math.
check: Prime a non-neutral HSL recipe, move only Whites on the same direct source, and compare the settled picture with a forced cold selection at the identical final grade. Repeat with a Local hue mask.
notes: Patch intentionally not written in Phase 2.

summary: The picker synchronizes the same global edit state twice before sending one post-release sampling request.
evidence: hslPickSamples awaits syncGlobalEditState then calls hslFetchStage, which awaits syncGlobalEditState and editCommandQueue again. Pointer moves only collect coordinates, so there is no GPU readback or backend request per pointer move.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; likely below the 15 ms audit floor when clean. Retaining one save fence is more important than eliminating this small duplicate.
proposed_fix: Keep one guarded save and revision fence in hslFetchStage; trace whether it saves any actual work first.
check: Add a picker release-to-colour-selected probe alongside the HSL own-control step; use hsl-picker-speed.js for coverage.

summary: Tiled HSL rebuilds selection from scratch for every tile even during HSL slider edits that do not change coverage.
evidence: Main and Clarity tile calls pass no prepareKey, unlike the direct route. Each tile encodes the fields pass, four preparation dispatches and three selection dispatches for a one-layer recipe without edge shaping; output storage is overwritten by the next tile.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; highest potential on warm HSL saturation drags forced to tiled rendering. A material gain is plausible if the selection passes dominate, but persistent mask storage could be worse on the Neo.
proposed_fix: Measure the direct and tiled routes separately, then assess bounded visible-tile mask reuse keyed by source generation, upstream grade, region and mask settings. Do not retain full-frame scratch.
check: HSL own Saturation drag at Fit on both photos; add large/100% or forced tiled only if Fit does not exercise it. Compare first feedback, settle and peak memory.

summary: Show selection repeats CPU guide preparation and PNG transfer after range changes and even after edits that leave coverage unchanged.
evidence: renderHslPanels keys refresh on editRevision/globalEditGeneration, and hslEnd submits a detailed request even when only hue, saturation or luminance changed. hslDrainSelection serializes requests, so release can wait behind one obsolete draft. sample_stage caches only upstream RGB, then redoes selection preparation, selection, PNG/base64 and browser decode.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; removing a needless refresh eliminates the whole overlay wait and contention for that edit. For actual range changes the saving is the prepare share plus any obsolete draft still in flight.
proposed_fix: Key refreshes on visible selection inputs, not every grade revision. Reuse prepared data only for the same stage identity, region and scale within the existing memory allowance.
check: Extra HSL own-control probe with Show selection enabled: change Saturation, wheels and Vignette (no request expected); then Range/Feather and Exposure (refresh expected). Compare release-to-exact overlay and the prepare/select/encode breakdown.

summary: Global HSL picking and Show selection sample the un-denoised picture even when the rendered HSL selects the denoised one.
evidence: sample_stage uses cache.hsl_stage_input, which calls capture_stage_input from raw proxies without a source_filter; the direct GPU fields pass binds sourceProxy after Denoise resolution and tiled HSL uses the denoised tile. The sample request carries adjustments but no Denoise selection state. In noisy or heavily cleaned regions the selected hue and mask can differ.
proposed_fix: Resolve which Denoise source/approximation the picker should represent and share that identity with the selection endpoint; no additional GPU readback on the drag path without evidence.
check: Compare Show selection and a strong HSL luminance grade on the same noisy crop with Denoise off/on; verify the picker tracks what the grade actually selects.
notes: Patch intentionally not written in Phase 2.

summary: Turning HSL off does not release its large, grow-only GPU work textures.
evidence: Per-canvas direct and tiled engines retain capacity up to their largest width, height and layer count; disabling HSL returns before ensure and leaves allocations alive. releaseHslSelection is on transient-resource teardown. A one-layer engine holds 80 bytes per work pixel plus coarse data (about 320 MB at 4 megapixels), and each additional layer adds 16 bytes per pixel.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; mostly a memory-headroom benefit, potentially avoiding slower routes under pressure. No expected speedup for a warm HSL-on frame by itself.
proposed_fix: Measure residency and route changes first; release inactive scratch under pressure or after an idle delay, keeping resources alive until fenced.
check: HSL own eye on/off and warm Denoise toggle at large/Fit; inspect idle GPU bytes and route before ON, after OFF and after re-enable. The interleaved OFF timings are not a cold-memory baseline.

summary: A nonzero Black & White mix adds 25 neighbouring texture reads per pixel before the normal grade, even when only Exposure or Contrast is being dragged.
evidence: The guided path samples a clamped 5×5 source lattice, then runs the upstream colour/tone prefix for the pixel and its guide. HSL fields repeats it in its own pass when stacked. With B&W neutral or off, the guide is skipped. Denoise changes the source the guide reads.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; a warm guide reuse could remove most of the incremental B&W cost on Exposure/Contrast or Reds drags if texture loads dominate; a Denoise source swap is a legitimate miss.
proposed_fix: Compare the existing fused path with source-keyed guide reuse only if material. Preserve the same tap ordering and do not grow the memory budget; measure before any separate pass.
check: B&W Exposure/Contrast ON vs OFF, Reds own drag, and Denoise toggle on/off. Separate warm render cost from first guide computation and check settled pixel parity.

summary: The shared-mask shader still evaluates each pixel's analytical hue-range coverage even when only the shared mask is used.
evidence: applyHsl loops all ranges, evaluates smoothsteps and creates circular target vectors, then replaces weight with hslSharedCoverage. With shared selection and Uniformity 0, the loop serves neither coverage nor target. CPU _apply_recipe_strip similarly computes full analytical weights and Oklab for every active channel before replacing weights.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; likely below the audit floor for an isolated one-range seed, but the saving scales with active channels and up to 32 ranges per channel on every Exposure/Contrast and Denoise render.
proposed_fix: Skip analytical coverage when the shared mask supplies it and skip target computation when Uniformity is zero; preserve the fallback and exact hue arithmetic. Consider a matching CPU cleanup separately.
check: HSL own Saturation and Exposure/Contrast ON/OFF at Fit with the normal seed and a separate multi-range stack, then the existing HSL preview/delivery pixel checks.

summary: Dragging a wheel puck updates every grade control on every pointer move and bypasses the normal gesture pacing.
evidence: The puck handler calls syncControlsFromState (including geometry, all ranges and Vignette layout) synchronously, then invalidates/schedules the preview without beginInteraction or endInteraction. Native ranges and HSL wheel handlers bracket their drags. pacedPreviewInteraction requires interacting to preserve a frame when HSL or Denoise are stacked.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; isolated drag gain may be under 15 ms, but with HSL or Denoise stacked, proper pacing could prevent missed feedback during the drag. Test separately from the Blending slider.
proposed_fix: Synchronize only the current wheel fields and modified indicators per frame. Bracket the actual pointer capture lifetime with existing preview pacing, and separately verify single-gesture undo before changing history semantics.
check: Native Shadows puck own-control drag at Fit; add a stacked HSL or Denoise pass, compare first feedback and settled output, and verify one Undo restores the initial puck.

summary: The Vignette outline does layout reads when hidden and rebuilds both paths even when Amount does not change the shape.
evidence: renderVignetteShape reads pane and image rectangles before its visibility test. The group input listener unconditionally calls it, and a visible outline generates two 96-point SVG paths per event, though Amount and highlight protection do not enter their coordinates.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; likely below 15 ms in isolation, with most potential on repeated visible-overlay Amount moves. No extra preview texture or GPU pass was found.
proposed_fix: Short-circuit hidden state before layout and separate positioning from path updates keyed by the geometric inputs only.
check: Vignette Amount own drag with overlay off and on; check same outline and current geometry while moving Midpoint or the centre.

summary: Active Color recomputes the same primaries matrix even when the changed control cannot affect the matrix.
evidence: Color activation from tint or Saturation calls rgbPrimariesAdjustmentMatrix during every buildParams, as do unrelated Exposure/Contrast renders. The matrix depends only on the eight hue/purity fields, not tint, temperature or saturation. Colour itself is a fused pointwise shader path, not a rebuilding LUT or an extra pass.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; likely below the audit floor. Only consider if buildParams is hot in a real trace.
proposed_fix: Reuse the exact same computed nine floats for unchanged primaries using a tiny bounded memo or last-value cache. Do not replace it with a different numerical shortcut.
check: Color own Saturation and Exposure/Contrast ON/OFF at Fit. Profile buildParams and verify identical packed values after an unrelated change.

summary: The Color seed is rejected because tint 8 exceeds the backend maximum of 2.
evidence: applyChanges sends the complete adjustment state to the backend. Model validation rejects tint 8. A replacement with saturation +0.45, tint +0.40 and temperature 4500 K changed at least one display channel by over 2 percentage points in 10.3% of Canon and 29.5% of Sony 480px CPU proxy pixels.
proposed_fix: Seed saturation .45, tint .40 and white_balance_kelvin 4500. Keep the Color eye and use a native Saturation drag as primary; Temperature or Tint can be secondary.
check: Phase 3 Fit on IMG_7723.CR3 and DSC00636.ARW. Require acknowledged seed and distinct fresh settled ON/OFF signatures. CPU proxy display is only a visibility sanity check.

summary: The current tint-only Wheels seed produces a weak signature on both photos, and Blending misses the actual wheel gesture.
evidence: The stock seed had p95 maximum-channel change of only 0.9/0.7 display points on Canon/Sony CPU proxies. Adding Shadows +0.40 EV and Highlights +0.35 EV moved 77.2%/56.0% of proxy pixels by over 2 points. The existing canvas drag helper is hard-wired to the curve editor.
proposed_fix: Seed Shadows hue 220°, saturation 28%, luminance +0.40 EV and Highlights hue 38°, saturation 18%, luminance +0.35 EV. Keep the Wheels eye. Drag the Shadows puck from its live centre by a fixed offset using the existing trusted-pointer timing path with a wheel-specific drag geometry. Keep Blending as a fallback, labelled as such.
check: Run both photos at Fit, confirming settled ON/OFF signatures and actual hue/saturation movement at the end of the native puck drag.

summary: The HSL recipe uses an invalid hue_shift property and the legal part of the red-only seed is too narrow for these photos.
evidence: seed merges hue_shift into the live recipe but both shader packing and the UI use hue; backend HSLRecipe forbids extra keys. The legal default-red/Saturation +48 seed changed neither 480px proxy by over 2 display points. The proposed broad recipe did so on 57.9% of Canon and 36.4% of Sony pixels.
proposed_fix: Keep channel red with one broad range {center:110,width:155,feather:24,subtract:false}, hue:12, saturation:48, luminance:.75, default spatial settings. Acknowledge the recipe before measuring. Keep the HSL eye; use native Saturation drag to exercise reuse and a separate range handle drag with Show selection on to exercise mask updates.
check: Run both photos at Fit and check first feedback, settle and ON/OFF signatures. Separately check overlay draft/exact advance and the warm masking route.

summary: The installed B&W seed is suitable, but its ON/OFF pixel change alone cannot prove the guided mix was applied.
evidence: B&W enabled with Reds +40 changes 58.9%/40.9% of Canon/Sony CPU proxy pixels by over 2 display points versus bypass. Neutral monochrome would also change pixels; Reds must be nonzero to invoke the lattice guide.
proposed_fix: Keep B&W enabled and Reds +40, use the B&W eye for OFF, and use native #bw-reds drag. Verify Reds is nonzero before each ON probe. Optionally compare neutral monochrome to Reds +40 separately to isolate guide cost.
check: Both photos at Fit: B&W own eye and Reds drag plus Exposure/Contrast and Denoise probes. Check ON has guided B&W enabled and OFF disables the guide without clearing settings.

summary: The existing Vignette seed is visibly non-neutral on both photos and its percent units must be kept.
evidence: Amount −45 and Midpoint 30 moved 64.3%/62.5% of Canon/Sony CPU proxy pixels by over 2 display points. Saved Amount uses percentage units, so −45 means −0.90 EV at full coverage and −0.4 would be nearly neutral.
proposed_fix: Keep amount:-45, midpoint:30 with current midpoint scale version, the Vignette eye, and a native Amount drag. Keep Show overlay off for the baseline and exercise it only in a separate UI probe.
check: Both photos at Fit: check settled centre and corner differences between ON/OFF and confirm eye restores the seed without needing to edit recipe values.

notes: M3-8 covers global packed bands. R5-6 already tracks the wider fix. R5-7 separately tracks cancelled encoders publishing unwritten bands.
summary: Tiled Clarity and packed Detail can reuse analysis of the wrong input after editing an already-enabled curve or changing Denoise.
evidence: The new curve LUT is uploaded independently of packed uniforms. Clarity coverage keys the uniforms, proxy epoch and Denoise controls, not the active global LUT or reconstruction variant. Global and local packed bands also omit actual Denoise identity and LUT contents. Global-to-local candidate keys omit effective global curve shape, and local curve offsets can stay fixed as shape changes.
proposed_fix: Use the effective upstream curve and resolved-input fingerprints for each cache. Fix separately from unsubmitted texture lifetime.
check: Repeat an active-curve move at 100% with Clarity only, then local Sharpen, and compare warm versus cold. Repeat Detail seeded with a primed Denoise ON/OFF pair and compare warm versus cold at fixed source and crop.

felt_impact: High candidate on Film-enabled Tone input: removing a substantial fraction of miss-path submits/work could save tens to hundreds of milliseconds end-to-end, unmeasured. Pan-only cache reuse benefits only coverage expansion.
summary: Post-lens Film controls can reuse the exact lens sum, but upstream Exposure or Contrast invalidates it and schedules 55 optical passes per rendered region.
evidence: The lens cache correctly includes the incoming grade. On miss the encoder extracts once and performs 27 horizontal and 27 accumulating vertical passes on the reduced spatial grid. Lens Strength can reuse the unmixed sum, but the other stages still run. Tone changes cannot reuse the old sum through nonlinear upstream grading. The tiled key also includes a whole-map coverage version for Clarity, so filling a distant map region can evict already-correct glow tiles.
proposed_fix: Keep real Tone dependencies. Profile the exact miss path before changing its dispatch organization. If pan misses are material, track local dependency or keep validated glow across coverage-only map growth where the sampled halo is already complete.
check: Film large Fit and 100%, paired exposure/contrast probes and own Lens Strength drag. Compare lens-glow reused=false/true, then run warm 100% pan with Detail Clarity active for the coverage case. Keep all fixed lens guards.

felt_impact: Likely below the 15 ms audit noise at a short radius; potentially tens of milliseconds of whole wait on a large view with a wide radius. Not measured.
summary: Halation extract and both broad blur passes run again even when only a downstream Film control changes.
evidence: The spatial function always writes extract, horizontal and vertical when Halation is enabled. The extract uses the pre-negative picture after lens and resolution scatter, plus physical radius/gate. Halation Amount and tint are applied only after the blur, and grain/print/scan controls are downstream. A Tone drag really changes this blur input; a downstream-only drag does not. The existing two ping-pong textures can be overwritten by lens work, and tiled scratch is reused between tiles.
proposed_fix: Measure first. Prototype an exact bounded pre-halation fingerprint and reuse the blurred alpha only for unchanged input, matching dimensions/grid, radius and halo. Prefer the current scratch allocation for a direct-only experiment; do not keep an unbounded tiled cache.
check: Film own Halation Amount and Grain Amount drags at large Fit and 100%; check smaller delta than upstream exposure/contrast only when blur is wide enough. Add a high-radius diagnostic if the default seed cannot resolve the cost. Compare finished pixels with the Film guards unchanged.

felt_impact: Two full-size passes and up to 16 bytes/pixel of Direct scratch are avoidable for Clarity-only. Expect tens of milliseconds on large processed views if the passes are a material share; unmeasured.
summary: Direct preview reruns both packed Detail blur passes even for a Clarity-only edit, and still does them when Clarity is the only enabled control.
evidence: Global graphActivity includes Clarity, and Direct unconditionally runs both packed-band passes whenever detailActive. Tiled global has the same unconditional pack/assemble path. The composite reads only the separate brightness map for Clarity. Texture-only and Sharpen-only likewise build all three packed components, rather than just their active components, though retained bands need explicit validity if a new component is enabled.
proposed_fix: Start with a true Clarity-only bypass for both routes and count scratch only when required. For combined controls, measure reuse of Direct bands on consumer-only amount/threshold drags and retain the current math and precision.
check: Detail own Clarity and Sharpen at large Fit and 100%. Add a Clarity-only diagnostic and compare against identical finished bytes after a cold render; exercise adding Texture/Sharpen before and after the bypass.

felt_impact: Highest Fit settle candidate: Nov 16 bounds combined grain cost at roughly 0.32–0.52 s on the cited grade, not a saving forecast for these two photos. A downstream-only cache could save a substantial fraction on a hit, zero when Tone changes the grain development input.
summary: Exact Fit Film recomputes its deterministic physical grain for every redrawn pixel, including on downstream-only edits.
evidence: Grain development depends on the pre-negative film input, coordinate, gate, seed and grain recipe. Exact reduced rendering can gather 16 sub-samples per pixel; native scale uses one, and interactive preview can use one. The field does not change randomly between frames. Nov 16 Neo evidence on a different saved grade puts finished 1024-edge waits at .405–.571 s with grain versus .054–.084 s without it. Exact density grain is not invariant under Tone but potentially invariant under downstream finishing changes.
proposed_fix: First profile exact stage and cache memory. Consider narrowly reusing an exact intermediate for scan/Lab controls or preserving reusable grain work only if current rounding and precision are preserved. Do not cache a static noise image in lieu of exposure-dependent grain; do not relax draft, export, Proof or parity requirements.
check: Film large Fit own Look/Grain and paired Tone/Denoise probes for exact grain load, then an own Scan Sharpening drag for potential downstream reuse. Compare at 100% as a native-scale control.

notes: Source trace, not visually reproduced. Phase 2 only permits findings file, so no patch was produced.
summary: At native zoom the tiled global Clarity prepass can fill too little source for later spatial effects, and can reduce wrongly clamped base-grade samples at chunk edges.
evidence: Map coverage starts at the pending tiles’ core bounds and expands only by Clarity reach. Lens/Halation/Structure and local Detail consume Clarity in the halo beyond the cores. Adding a long Film reach to a narrow Clarity map exposes samples whose map support was not filled. Separately the prepass computes base grade over exactly each reduction chunk, without an input guard for earlier BW and HSL neighbours; shader reads clamp at scratch bounds. roiSourceHalo takes a max of reach provisions rather than planning both these dependencies together.
proposed_fix: Plan coverage from the portion of Clarity output later passes read, and pad the source of each reduction chunk for BW/HSL/Denoise as required while writing only its interior texels. Share this plan with ROI source fetch and account for scratch.
check: At 100% compare cold ROI vs whole-frame tiled and warm pan-return with Clarity plus wide Lens/Halation. Separately test Clarity and active BW mix or HSL Shared Selection on chunk edges, versus fixed-resolution Direct and CPU. Keep all guards intact.

notes: Confirmed with a standalone Node arithmetic check at 8660×5784: the planner returns 272, while the shader’s leftmost read is −275. Not measured on GPU. Phase 2 only permits findings file, so no patch was produced.
summary: Halation’s tile halo omits bilinear sampling support when no Lens Filter is active.
evidence: At spatial grid 4, an interior tile’s first pixel x=0 relative to its core samples spatial texel -1 as well as 0. With a capped 64-texel blur, texel -1 needs extract texel -65. Its earliest integer extract sample is -259, and the capped 16-pixel edge detector reads -275. The Halation-only planner reserves 64*4+16=272, so the last needed neighbour clamps to the tile edge. The extra grid texel in the reach formula is reserved only for Lens, not for Halation’s own interpolation; with both stages active each reconstruction has its own support.
proposed_fix: Derive extraction and bilinear reach for every stage from its actual read coordinates and add the two reaches where chained, preserving existing physical caps.
check: Large 100% Film with Lens None, wide capped Halation, a synthetic bright edge aligned to the first or last few pixels of a tile; compare Direct vs Tiled with existing Film guards and repeat with Lens enabled.

felt_impact: Potentially large only near admission pressure or fallback. Expect negligible latency change with headroom, but 16 bytes per processed pixel of optional retained Direct scratch and bounded tile-cache residency are worth isolating. No measured memory bug.
summary: Detail scratch remains resident after bypass and its packed tile cache can compete with the native zoom working set.
evidence: At 50 MP, one RGBA16F texture is 400 MB. Direct would ask for four frame textures (1.6 GB) plus two Detail surfaces (800 MB), two quarter-grid Film surfaces (50 MB) and optional glow (25 MB), excluding source, presentation, caches and Clarity. Normal Full/100% admission is tiled or ROI, so those are not actual observed 100% allocations. Tiled scratch is halo-sized and reused; the 512² packed bands cost 2 MiB per cached tile and the 50 MP full-frame equivalent is ~400 MB per scope if untrimmed. Direct reuses and retains the Detail pair after a module-off draw; existing ceilings/eviction must be preserved. Tiled allocates six RGBA16F work surfaces including two Detail surfaces even for an inactive module, plus one source and optional denoised surface and spatial pair. At 512 with no halo a half-float source plus six surfaces is 14 MiB; a 272-pixel halo on each side with the same source and quarter grid pair costs ~61 MiB, excluding optional outputs and caches.
proposed_fix: Start by avoiding scratch for Clarity-only. If the ON-to-OFF idle footprint is material and route transitions reclaim too late, release optional Direct pairs under existing reclaim signals; preserve warm reuse when affordable. Measure active scopes and tile cache eviction separately.
check: Detail eye and paired Tone/Denoise probes at large Fit/100%; report route, processed edge, idle/peak allocator bytes, renderer/GPU physical footprint, and detail cache bytes. Compare ON to OFF in both orders.

felt_impact: One to three RGBA16F copies eliminated per rendered region. Likely few milliseconds at Fit, potentially tens at large viewport/catch-up. Lower priority than bad cache misses or grain.
summary: The Film chain schedules two full-size identity draws even on a simple no-structure frame.
evidence: filmResponseFragmentMain only textureLoads. encodeFilmChain first copies original into filmTexture before any neighborhood processing and finally copies scan output from filmTexture to finishTexture whenever structure is off or diagnostic-map mode is on. The lens-only branch adds another full-size identity draw after mixing. These copies preserve existing graph roles, but have no independent image math.
proposed_fix: Profile on device before changing graph roles. Experiment with passing the existing source view into the next stage and routing the last scan to the final target when it is not also an input. Retain all numerical store boundaries and strict comparisons.
check: Film eye and paired Exposure/Contrast Fit and 100%; instrument pass count and first feedback/settle versus same exact finished pixels. Include Film off, Lens only, diagnostic map, and Softness/Microcontrast on.

felt_impact: Avoids an entire redundant scheduled preview when open/unchanged close would otherwise reach encode, potentially one full graded frame of work. The existing debounce can coalesce short interactions, so there may be no noticeable gain on a single fast click.
summary: Film Stock picker focus is a real Grade preview, and focusing or closing on an unchanged option still retires and reschedules a frame.
evidence: There is no thumbnail job in this file: every focus calls choose, clones the entire opening recipe, and invalidates and debounces the active lane. The opening value still takes that path. restore unconditionally invalidates too. Unchanged focus/close and repeated focus of the same option can supersede in-flight work without any pixel change; a moving highlight may have to run Film exact if it settles. Cold selections may also await a full stock table fetch via renderToFrame; after load its packed stock slot is reused.
proposed_fix: Track the last applied option and whether any temporary recipe has changed. Skip invalidation for identical focus and untouched close. Preserve Escape restore, session/lane guards, forced retirement when pixels really changed, and one-entry undo.
check: Outside the standard matrix, profile own Film picker at Fit and 100% for open/close unchanged and rapid arrows then Escape. Count accepted and superseded renders; verify stock picker commit/cancel and history tests.

summary: Clarity’s retained GPU map allocations are missing from the resident memory ledger.
evidence: Each clarityMaps entry creates and retains three RG16F textures and only calls recordAllocation, which adds an instrumentation event when enabled, not an allocator reservation. resourceMemorySnapshot counts neither maps nor the separately captured surround textures. At 8660×5784 with base scale 4 the tiled map’s three textures account for about 37.6 MB before alignment; frame, analysis-frame, work and local scratch entries can coexist. This does not prove a ceiling violation.
proposed_fix: Budget persistent map growth under the existing memory limit and include live retained/deferred-release allocations exactly once in the allocator and diagnostics. Keep the current processing scale and memory ceilings.
check: Detail eye at large Fit and 100%, with Clarity on and with an anchor measuring in parallel. Compare map allocation events against gpuSnapshot bytes and physical footprint; verify cleanup at session reset and resize.

felt_impact: A clean miss already costs roughly 65 ms in isolated backend work, before parse/upload. Saving much of that could improve input-to-screen by tens of milliseconds or more on first-pass Print Contrast drags. Warm cache hits save little.
summary: Print Contrast sends megabytes of unchanged film tables for each newly sampled slider value, before the preview can draw.
evidence: The query key contains exact Contrast, Shadows and Highlights values; there are only eight variant slots.
