The backend caches a few computed curves but re-expands the base manifest, copies the full scanner table and serializes the entire payload for each uncached UI request. With Portra 400, exact contrast +20 and +24 emitted 4.38 MB of compact JSON each in a CPU-only spot check. Backend payload construction plus stdlib compact JSON serialization took about 65 ms each on this machine, excluding HTTP, renderer parse/pack/upload and GPU. renderToFrame awaits the stock request before drawing.
proposed_fix: Measure the drag. On a win, reuse the already-loaded immutable stock data and transfer only the variant print curve or legitimately changed scanner values. Preserve bytes and precision when packing the variant and leave delivery independent of transport optimization.
check: Add Film own Print Contrast at Fit and 100%, report cold and warm reruns separately, and break down request wait, payload size, GPU submission and first feedback/settle. Keep stock/paper/Lab qualification and fixed film/lens guards.

notes: Request poisoning and slot 0 reproduced without Electron. Visual and Proof effects are source-traced. Phase 2 only permits findings file, so no patch was produced.
summary: A single transient stock-table request failure can keep a selected Film stock visually missing for the rest of the frontend session.
evidence: Network errors, non-OK response codes and packing failures all enter the same permanent failed Set. Further requests for the exact key return early: slot remains 0, and the shader skips the measured response while other Film effects can continue. renderToFrame awaits a promise whose catch swallows the failure after logging, so it can present a frame without the named stock. This also applies to a single Print/Lab variant. Confirmed in a CPU-only Node stub: after one HTTP 503, requesting Portra Contrast +20 again makes no second fetch and slot() reports 0.
proposed_fix: Distinguish transient failures from permanent missing or invalid stock data. Retain a valid presentation or take the existing qualified fallback, and allow a bounded retry of transient table loads. Do not add UI or relax parity.
check: Use a fetch stub that fails once and succeeds, including a controlled Print variant. Verify no unqualified stock-less frame is accepted as exact and that the chosen look recovers. Audit existing Proof fallback if it shares this request.

summary: The current Detail audit changes pixels on both RAWs but is subtle at Fit and does not directly drag the radius cache path.
evidence: 1024-edge CPU-rendered HDR-to-SDR display RGB versus default, max-channel 8-bit delta: existing seed changes 62.16% of Canon IMG_7723.CR3 and 76.91% of Sony DSC00636.ARW pixels; 2.24% and 1.74% move by at least 3 codes. The proposed recipe gives 66.73% and 82.01% changed, with 9.06% and 7.28% moving by at least 3 codes. Clarity and Sharpen Amount are representative existing drags; neither samples the radius-dependent Clarity map blur in isolation.
proposed_fix: Seed Detail eye on, texture_amount=25, clarity_amount=50 (coefficient +0.40), clarity_radius_percent=0.75, sharpen_amount=50 (coefficient 0.50), sharpen_radius_px=0.8, sharpen_threshold=0, softness=0, microcontrast=0. Keep own Clarity and Sharpen drags and add Clarity Radius if the time budget permits; use a separate Clarity-only diagnostic for packed-band bypass, and a separate Softness or Microcontrast drag if measuring Film finishing.
check: H3/Phase 3 at Fit on both RAWs and at large 100%: validate live ON/OFF pixelsChanged and native slider events, including an own Clarity Radius drag. CPU spot-check is not GPU presentation or perceptual qualification.

summary: The Portra audit recipe makes a clear change on both RAWs, but current own drags miss the print-table path and the scan stage.
evidence: 1024-edge CPU-rendered HDR-to-SDR display versus default: existing recipe moves at least 3 max-channel RGB8 codes on 93.81% of Canon IMG_7723.CR3 and 76.08% of Sony DSC00636.ARW pixels; proposed recipe reaches 94.79% and 89.44%. Look Strength, Lens Strength, Halation Amount and Grain Amount are representative respective paths. They do not build controlled print tables, and default zero Scan Sharpening does not exercise its kernel. Direct recipe assignment does not run Film stock inheritance; these are resolved renderer values, not stock-relative UI percentages.
proposed_fix: Seed Film eye on with default resolved lane values plus film_stock=kodak_portra_400, look_strength=80, lens_filter=black_pro_mist, lens_strength=0.30, lens_size=1, halation_enabled=true, halation_amount=25, halation_radius=0.20, grain_enabled=true, grain_amount=28, film_resolution=90, print_contrast=20, scan_sharpening=25. Keep current own drags and prioritize Print Contrast. Add Scan Sharpening at 100%: on a sufficiently reduced Fit proxy the kernel rounds to radius zero.
check: H3/Phase 3 verify HDR-lane pixelsChanged at Fit on both RAWs and 100% on large; include own Print Contrast, plus Scan Sharpening at large 100% if budget allows. Use a separate capped-radius Halation check for edge correctness and wide-blur timing; do not make it the routine seed. CPU spot-check did not test live presentation.

summary: Local measures an implicit Fit-only gesture recipe and can click outside the viewport at 100%.
evidence: The helper chooses 30%/40% to 70%/60% of the entire image rectangle, not its visible intersection; both tools get Exposure only and their positions and settings are absent from the recipe hash.
proposed_fix: Seed at Fit for both audit zooms. In HDR set brush stroke (.30,.40) to (.70,.60), seven equal samples including endpoints, 100%-pressure mouse, brush radius .025 (Size 5.0%), hardness .75, flow/opacity 1, smoothing .35, Exposure +0.80 EV and Saturation +0.25. Draw linear gradient (.30,.40) to (.70,.60), Exposure -0.55 EV and Saturation -0.20. Store these values in the recipe, then return to the requested zoom. OFF uses the Local eye.
check: On IMG_7723.CR3 and DSC00636.ARW compare brush only, gradient only and both to bypass, using picture pixels at Fit and large at 100% with the overlay turned off.
notes: CPU-only sanity check using half-resolution LibRaw decode of both RAWs reduced to 384 px: max RGB channel shift above 0.0001 on 3.46% of pixels for brush and 74.66–74.67% for gradient. This is not GPU or live-driver validation.

summary: The two Heal donors change source position between Fit and 100%.
evidence: The driver clips the image rectangle to the viewer then uses its fractions as click positions. The app interprets clicks in the full image rectangle, then maps to native source coordinates.
proposed_fix: At Fit and neutral geometry create two Heals at full-image normalized donor→destination (.38,.44)→(.50,.50) and (.57,.50)→(.66,.56), diameter 128 native px, feather 25%, texture 100%, opacity 100%. Return to requested zoom after creation. OFF disables both eyes. Keep Clean Grain for the timed probes and report Micro Grain unavailable with enabled repairs.
check: Compare pre-overlay pixels around both targets with ON and OFF on both RAWs at Fit and use a target-centered or explicitly framed 100% proof on DSC00636.ARW. Confirm saved native points and size, and a configurable own-control probe selects a saved spot before Apply.
notes: CPU replay on the half-resolution LibRaw decode, scaling diameter to 64 px to match native coverage: both Heals on both RAWs changed 68.97–69.14% of pixels within the repair patches by over 0.0001 in at least one RGB channel. Live pointer placement and Fit visibility still need the driver.

summary: The Geometry audit seed never exercises the perspective warp.
evidence: perspective_rotate is added to straighten_angle in geometry_resample_stage. With horizontal and vertical at zero, the current seed is a 6° roll.
proposed_fix: HDR ON crop {x:.08,y:.08,width:.84,height:.84}, straighten_angle=2, perspective_horizontal=+12, perspective_vertical=0, perspective_rotate=0, quarter rotation and flips neutral. OFF restore the full crop and zeros, offMethod neutral.
check: On both RAWs at Fit and on DSC00636.ARW at 100%, assert backend geometry_resample_stage is perspective and validate picture pixel deltas. Record own straighten drag/apply.
notes: CPU-only sanity check on a 384x256 LibRaw-derived source for each RAW: proposed seed selects perspective and returns a resampled 309x199 frame. The existing roll-only seed also changes framing, but misses the required warp route.

summary: SDR Match OFF restores the defaults captured before seeding HDR, so it does not isolate the Match from its HDR setup.
evidence: Own-control samples reapply HDR seed before pressing Match, but moduleState(false) restores defaults rather than the same pre-Match HDR grade.
proposed_fix: In SDR lane seed HDR Exposure +0.35 EV, Contrast +0.12, Saturation +0.12. Save this pre-Match document with default SDR and Clean Grain disabled, click Match Entire, settle and capture matched document. OFF restores the pre-Match document, preserving the identical HDR seed; keep neutral restore semantics, not an eye.
check: Both RAWs at Fit. Assert HDR equality in ON/OFF, independent editable SDR Match recorded in ON and nonidentical picture pixels.
notes: CPU-only sanity check on 384 px LibRaw-derived sources: both fits returned matched and changed at least one RGB channel by over 0.0001 on every sampled pixel against pre-Match SDR. Real app still needs the GPU/CPU route and signature confirmation.

summary: A second small repair copies the full native RGB frame even though repair solving and changed output rectangles are bounded.
evidence: Incremental publication allocates an immutable full-size destination and copies all rows from the previous frame before patching dirty rectangles. At 50 MP a float32 RGB frame is about 600 MB; original, old repaired and replacement can overlap at about 1.8 GB before proxies. Existing memory admission prevents unsafe allocation.
felt_impact: Estimated 0.1–0.5 s off whole repair settle when copy dominates, potentially more under paging, and ~600 MB less transient overlap if copy-free publication proves feasible. No gain expected on warmed downstream probes.
proposed_fix: First break down retouch_replay_timing copy_ms and footprint. Investigate using existing file-backed immutable owners or bounded patch windows in preview providers only if they remove a meaningful fraction of felt wait without changing source pixels or ownership.
check: Phase 3 large 100% own.retouch size/apply and eye with one enabled repair remaining; log copy_ms, actual settle and backend footprint.

summary: Repeated whole-proxy requests can rewarp the same already-developed mip.
evidence: The raw mip is reused by _proxies but the output of apply_geometry, the reduced-level clamp and downsample_image are not cached in geometry_source_proxy. HDR and generated SDR both choose the same source. New geometry legitimately needs a new transform; full RAW development is not repeated.
felt_impact: Estimated 60–350 ms off whole settle on duplicate reduced exact proxy requests with perspective, dependent on request overlap and tier. No savings for a lone cold geometry signature or native window extraction.
proposed_fix: Measure paired duplicate same-key requests. If material, coalesce them or reuse one budgeted immutable transformed result keyed by source epoch, authored source class, edge, geometry and screen mode. Preserve stale-request gates.
check: Phase 3 own.geometry.straighten.drag release→exact at 4K Fit and with dual lanes as a follow-up. Count transforms for equal keys and compare visible settle and peak footprint.

summary: The pre-pin pass uses an obsolete luminance-mask key, so one local can evict another mask still needed by the same frame.
evidence: loadGpuLumaMask stores keys with a :refinement:<feather>:<inverted> suffix, while markResidentMaskFrame looks up only the old base key. Per-entry retain immediately trims and skips only the current serial. Over the mask budget an unpinned resident luma mask may be rebuilt even for unchanged geometry and mask values.
felt_impact: Estimated 20–150 ms off current-frame settle under multipass luma cache pressure; zero for ordinary brush/gradient rows below budget. Larger effect possible when churn causes texture eviction or a fallback.
proposed_fix: Share the full key constructor between load and pre-pin, including region/refinement identity. Check that transient active-frame pinning still releases resources and obeys the aggregate budget.
check: Follow-up to Phase 3 large 100% probe.tone.exposure.drag and probe.tone.contrast.drag: add two different-feather luma locals plus enough active masks to trigger trimming; inspect baseRegenerated/refinementRan and memory.

summary: Whole SDR Match computes its target without enabled HDR Denoise and only copies those settings after fitting.
evidence: source_pair returns underlying repaired RAW proxy; current_denoise is deep-copied but not passed to materialize_sdr_match. sdr_match_inputs renders the pre-Denoise HDR target, then the commit mirrors HDR Denoise to SDR. The reported fit can therefore measure a different picture from the preview when grain/noise reduction changes it.
proposed_fix: Test the difference first. If material and approved, supply the authoritative lane-Denoised source inputs at the correct pipeline position for both fit and CPU certification, or document the approximation and do not claim settled-Denoised metrics.
check: Compare target and reported quality against the authoritative settled HDR/SDR rendering on IMG_0790.CR2 with high Clean Grain, then repeat with Denoise off.
notes: Phase 2 findings-only. No corrective patch. Current technical docs explicitly omit stochastic grain and describe a settled HDR picture; they do not say this target omits enabled Denoise.

summary: An explicit repeat of the same Match still runs the picture fit and CPU certification from scratch.
evidence: Ordinary Tone edits never call the Match action. Each explicit click snapshots inputs and calls materialize_sdr_match; fixed source, masks and metric target are reused within a fit only, not across identical actions. The audit's same repeated HDR seed exposes this cost.
felt_impact: Estimated 0.5–5 s off whole repeat-click settle if the fit dominates and an exact reusable result exists. The CPU-only 384 px LibRaw-derived sanity runs spent 4.82 and 5.43 s in fitting, not the user-visible path or a Mac GPU baseline.
proposed_fix: Measure repeat-click fit and post-fit render separately. If material, reuse only a small last CPU-certified fit for identical semantic inputs including source epoch, sections, pre-Match SDR dependencies and candidate route/quality mode; never bypass consent, revision checks, commit or delivery parity.
check: Retain cold own.sdr_match.entire.click as the primary result and add a repeat-identical-input row on both Fit photos with candidate count and settle. Compare resulting settings, quality and pixels exactly.

summary: A superseded Match can wait for a GPU candidate and then run an entire CPU fit that cannot be applied.
evidence: The UI candidate loop exits when the selected session changes. RemoteCandidateBridge waits up to 6 s for the first candidate or 3 s later. A refusal or timeout restarts on CPU without a freshness checkpoint; apply_sdr_match_action checks revision at commit only. Even without a candidate bridge the CPU run can outlive its inputs.
felt_impact: Up to 3–6 s of obsolete bridge wait plus the remaining fit, avoided on the discard path. Improvement to the next visible action is unmeasured and only expected if the obsolete fit competes for resources, not in the ordinary successful click.
proposed_fix: Propagate a session/revision staleness signal through candidate wait and CPU render iterations and distinguish cancellation from renderer failure. Keep the single CPU retry for a real failure of a current request.
check: Follow-up to own.sdr_match.entire.click: switch photo or commit a newer HDR edit while the bridge awaits a candidate, assert no obsolete CPU restart and measure next-photo first feedback/settle.

summary: Grade announces ordinary Heal and Clone work as a GPU failure.
evidence: solve_record marks the intended CPU Heal/Clone route with no fallback_reason, but renderRetouchRoute selects all CPU records and emits a persistent Retouch CPU fallback notice. The product spec and delivery notice select only actual failures.
proposed_fix: Filter on nonempty fallback_reason, keeping the existing status text for real Inpaint failure.
check: Add a normal Heal, a normal Clone and a forced Inpaint fallback; only the last must show the notice. Check undo and photo switch clear it.
notes: Phase 2 findings-only. No corrective patch.

summary: Renaming an enabled repair dirties the renderer's source, local masks and both Denoise preparations without changing pixels.
evidence: The function compares full repair JSON first, so a name-only edit enters and increments repairSourceGeneration, clears overlay masks and invalidates both lanes' Denoise. The meaningful recipe comparison for dirty windows happens only after invalidation and returns no changed repairs. Backend already retains native pixels for name-only edits.
felt_impact: Estimated near zero with Denoise off in a simple scene, 0.2–2 s off visible settle or next Denoise enable if a warm large preparation is needlessly rebuilt. Confirm against real route timings before prioritizing.
proposed_fix: Gate source and preparation invalidation on an actual pixel-source change, including enabled order and source epoch. Preserve name updates and undo/redo in the edit document.
check: Follow-up to large 100% probe.denoise.toggle_on and probe.denoise.toggle_off with Retouch ON: prime Clean Grain, rename a spot, repeat timed toggles. Verify no extra source epoch, mask compile, or Denoise preparation rebuild for rename, undo, and redo.

summary: Mask preparation diagnostics can grow for a whole renderer lifetime even with instrumentation disabled.
evidence: Several loaders append maskEvents unconditionally; only the instrumented luma path imposes the 480-event cap, and setInstrumentationEnabled resets it only when explicitly enabled. A long pan/paint/geometry session generating tiled masks accrues extra JS objects even as the texture cache evicts them.
proposed_fix: Use one bounded mask event recorder that respects instrumentation or keeps a bounded recent history if a consumer needs default visibility.
check: Add a CPU-only recorder test and pan/paint a 50 MP transformed frame in an instrumented follow-up; cap events without dropping the newest evidence.

summary: Retouch keeps a full serialized recipe as the route diagnostic key for each superseded edit until the session closes.
evidence: _repair_routes accumulates keys for solved recipes, including up to 512 samples plus donor-exclusion strokes, independent of the bounded completed-patch cache and edit-history retention. records only exposes entries for active recipes.
proposed_fix: Bound route metadata to the reachable repairs/history or use compact recipe digests with bounded retention. Do not alter diagnostic behavior when undoing a still-reachable repair.
check: Repeatedly modify and undo a long repair in the same session. Confirm route metadata stays bounded and actual fallback reasons still display for reachable history.

summary: Failure to initialize the diagnostic log aborts startup before its error handler and can block shutdown.
evidence: With logs occupied by an ordinary file, rotating-log creation throws. app.whenReady calls libraryStage before its startup try, and beginShutdown emits action_started before its cleanup try. The backend also tried to create the same directory again.
proposed_fix: Log initialization failure once to stderr, keep a discard writer, and reuse the logger path in backend startup.
check: node --test tests/rotating-log.test.js from codebase/desktop (4 passed, including a real initialization failure).

felt_impact: The app can keep processing window events during the disk wait. Selected file elapsed time was not measured.
summary: The portable grading-preset dialogs do selected file I/O synchronously on Electron's main thread, and export parses the same JSON three times.
evidence: The renderer uses invoke for the native dialogs. After a user selects a path, the main process waited synchronously on stat/read or write even on removable or remote storage. The handlers now wait asynchronously, preserving result bytes, cancellation and the existing import size limit.
proposed_fix: Use promise-based filesystem operations and parse the outgoing JSON once for the export name.
check: node --test tests/preset-file-ipc.test.js from codebase/desktop (2 passed).

summary: Malformed progress and diagnostic event fields can throw uncaught in Electron's fire-and-forget listeners.
evidence: preload uses ipcRenderer.send for both. Number() on a plain malformed progress field and RegExp.test() on malformed event/action fields throw before the listener returns. The regression tests reproduced both exceptions and passed after type validation.
proposed_fix: Accept numeric progress values and validate diagnostic string fields before running the regular expressions; keep existing fallbacks for invalid input.
check: Desktop progress-ipc and event-log (4 pass) and codebase diagnostics.test.js (4 pass).

summary: A failed startup splash load is silently discarded while the rest of startup continues.
evidence: The splash loads separately from the hidden editor. A rejected load leaves it invisible, with no error record to distinguish that from slow backend startup; the editor reveal is independent.
proposed_fix: Warn through stderr on a rejected load unless the splash is already closing, destroyed or shutting down.
check: node --test tests/splash-window.test.js from codebase/desktop (1 passed, rejects both live and closing splash loads).

summary: Saved grading presets can be hidden when presets from other groups fill the directory scan limit.
evidence: With 500 earlier HDR Tone files, an SDR Tone preset saved by the app and a hand-named SDR preset were omitted. The current limit is applied before grouping.
proposed_fix: Skip app-format filenames belonging to other known groups before taking the existing 500-file read limit. Keep payload validation and scan nonstandard names.
check: The grouping regression reproduced before and passed after the patch in scratch, including when rebased onto R1-15. The HDR group still returns all 500 entries.

summary: Export Grading Presets fails before opening the Save dialog in packaged builds.
evidence: The handler requires a sibling frontend module, but Electron Builder does not put it beside the app. The packaged-layout emulation failed with MODULE_NOT_FOUND on current code.
proposed_fix: Bundle the existing filename helper in shared and require it there in packaged builds. Keep existing preset bytes and filename rules.
check: The packaged-layout Node regression failed before the patch and passed after it; all three preset IPC tests passed. No native package was built.

summary: Cancelling Quit leaves it armed, so a later ordinary editor close can close the detached Library and quit the app.
evidence: Quit sets quitRequested. Project prompt cancellation, failed or abandoned close-save, and a sidecar cancellation do not reset it. The project and sidecar regressions reproduced a later unexpected shutdown.
proposed_fix: Clear quitRequested on direct cancellation and negative save or sidecar acknowledgement, but keep it while a requested save is pending.
check: Both added photo-close regressions failed before and passed after the patch; all seven photo-close tests passed in a scratch copy.

felt_impact: The shell can handle events while the storage responds. No whole-wait timings were measured.
summary: Library cache-folder discovery and reveal can block the main process on a filesystem probe or mkdir.
evidence: The Library settings query created and removed the portable-cache probe synchronously. Reveal ran mkdirSync on the configured folder before opening it.
proposed_fix: Await file creation, cleanup and directory creation asynchronously, keeping the same shell calls and result.
check: node --test tests/library-cache-ipc.test.js from codebase/desktop (2 passed).

felt_impact: Window events can still run during cache reads or writes. Network wait and disk latency were not measured.
summary: A startup or manual update check blocks the main thread when loading or writing its disk cache.
evidence: The startup and manual update commands share the same handler and both use synchronous filesystem calls. Read and write failures were ignored completely.
proposed_fix: Read asynchronously, serialize cache writes and log unexpected failures without changing update results.
check: node --test tests/update-cache.test.js tests/validation.test.js from codebase/desktop (12 passed).

summary: Settings and window bounds silently fall back to defaults when their stored JSON cannot be read.
evidence: Both catch blocks ignored read or parse errors. Existing fallbacks are correct, but troubleshooting cannot distinguish an unreadable or damaged file from normal first launch.
proposed_fix: Warn for failed restore operations except missing files, with no new UI and no change to the fallbacks.
check: node --test tests/settings-load.test.js tests/application-preferences.test.js tests/window-bounds.test.js tests/window-state-save.test.js from codebase/desktop (9 passed).

felt_impact: The shell can respond during the history disk wait. No whole-wait timing was measured.
summary: Opening or remembering a Recent project makes synchronous disk calls on the main process.
evidence: The recent-project list reads during the Open browser flow. Document state IPC rewrites the list on open/save using a read, mkdir, write and rename before returning.
proposed_fix: Queue asynchronous reads and atomic writes in request order, publish window state without waiting and flush history before quitting.
check: node --test codebase/tests/recent-projects.test.js codebase/desktop/tests/photo-close.test.js from ai (6 passed).

summary: A backend exit during its final health check can leave the editor connected to a dead process.
evidence: The readiness listener is removed after READY and the lasting exit monitor is added only after /health. If the child exits after sending a successful response but before the awaited JSON completes, logs and application state still claim it started.
proposed_fix: Check for an exited child after the health body and before publishing readiness; use the existing startup failure route.
check: Scratch Node test emitted child exit while health JSON completed. It failed before the patch and passed afterward (1 case).

felt_impact: The detached Library can stay on Preparing adjustments until the existing five-minute timeout.
summary: A detached Library paste can stay pending after the editor closes or its renderer crashes.
evidence: Only the editor acknowledgement and five-minute timeout retire the request. The Library sets its preparing state before awaiting approval, and renderer loss or window close does not retire it.
proposed_fix: Associate requests with both windows and resolve them as cancelled when either closes or its renderer exits.
check: Scratch Node test reproduced pending timers after requester loss, then checked prompt cancellation, late acknowledgement and unrelated requests with the patch (1 passed).

felt_impact: The shell can process events during path lookup. No whole-wait measurement was taken.
summary: Open and Save As check the selected project path synchronously in the main process.
evidence: The unified browser invokes the project grant handler for a path that can live on removable or network storage; the existence check ran before the asynchronous grant.
proposed_fix: Use an asynchronous existence check, preserving the open rejection and the save result.
check: node --test tests/project-grant-ipc.test.js from codebase/desktop (1 passed).

felt_impact: The shell can respond during file waits. No end-to-end preset latency change was measured.
notes: Preset directory creation and default resolution remain synchronous and are shared with Settings and Batch Export.
summary: Opening or editing a grading preset can block the desktop main thread on repeated filesystem calls.
evidence: A list may read up to 500 files synchronously and saves synchronously check, read, back up and overwrite files. Preset folders can be configured outside app storage.
proposed_fix: Await the listing, reads, writes and removal in invocation order, keeping sorting, cap, validation, backups and atomic rename. Wait for queued writes on quit.
check: 9 targeted desktop Node tests passed, including overlapping saves, exact JSON shape, backup, sorted listing and deletion. R1-5 still reproduces independently.

summary: A rejected backend-exit dialog or Windows session-end warning leaves no diagnostic.
evidence: Both existing dialogs swallowed rejection. Node exercised a rejected dialog in each path and verified dirty-project protection and no automatic quit.
proposed_fix: Write the rejection and its cause to the diagnostic console without altering the dialogs or close decisions.
check: node --test tests/lifecycle-dialog.test.js tests/process-diagnostics.test.js from codebase/desktop (5 passed).

notes: No whole-wait slowdown was measured. Candidate patch serializes preference writes and menu publication; left open until felt impact and real app behavior are verified.
summary: Changing application settings or rendering mode still performs a synchronous preferences write on the main thread.
evidence: Renderer Settings and the native rendering-mode menu both call mkdir, write and rename synchronously. The latter also synchronously rebuilds the menu and sends the chosen mode after the write.
proposed_fix: If end-to-end settings latency warrants it, serialize preference writes and add close-time draining without allowing IPC and menu state to overtake each other.
check: The scratch candidate preserved disk snapshot and menu order under delayed writes (1 Node test). Measure both UI actions and verify disk-error and quit behavior before applying.

notes: Strict export lifecycle path. The review patch is not applied.
summary: Desktop shutdown discards both delivery shutdown request failures and non-success responses.
evidence: The POST ignores transport errors and never inspects response.ok, then continues closing. A scratch Node test confirmed network error and HTTP 503 leave no trace.
proposed_fix: Warn on either failure while retaining the current timeout and backend cleanup order.
check: Three targeted Node cases passed against the proposed patch. Still requires delivery-path verification before applying.

summary: Library renderers keep running a 100 ms Grade activity timer that cannot report any activity.
evidence: Shared renderer initialization and ordinary Library draws start the timer; HDRLibraryGPU.reportDeliveryActivity always returns reserved:0 without an IPC or GPU call. The shared foreground wait therefore also exits immediately.
felt_impact: Removes up to ten idle callbacks per second per initialized Library renderer; no felt-wait gain measured.
proposed_fix: Clear the inherited timer after Library renderer initialization and stop restarting it on ordinary draws.
check: Node simulation draws a cached picture and verifies no timer remains; coordinator quick Library check covers actual renderer startup and draws.
notes: Four targeted Node files passed (24 tests).

summary: Overlay map decoding leaves the bitmap open if the canvas draw fails and relies on GC for the full temporary canvas backing even after successful readback.
evidence: The overlay loader decodes an ImageBitmap, then calls getContext/drawImage before close and never zeroes the scratch canvas. A mocked draw failure reaches the existing error handler without calling close on the baseline. The canvas is only needed to extract ImageData.
felt_impact: Reduces transient overlay memory retention; whole-wait benefit not measured.
proposed_fix: Close the bitmap before readback as before and guarantee cleanup of the bitmap and scratch canvas on all exits.
check: Overlay Node suite mocks a failed draw and a successful readback, checks both owners are released and the original success/error outcomes are preserved.
notes: 28 targeted overlay Node tests pass. Real-app Focus/Exposure smoke still needed.

summary: The periodic RAM report and explicit reclaim report can post out of order from the same Library window.
evidence: The timer guard only covers ticks. HDRLibraryReclaimWaiting and HDRLibraryCollectWaiting call report directly after trims, and backend memory_report overwrites the same renderer keys for every POST. A delayed older POST or response can replace newer byte counts or limits.
felt_impact: Avoids stale accounting after a reclaim; no whole-wait gain measured.
proposed_fix: Serialize per-window requests and sample the cache at send time; allow the next request after failures.
check: Delay the first POST, overlap a reclaim report, and verify ordered fresh byte counts and recovery after failure.
notes: Nine targeted RAM/monitor Node tests pass. Limits and both enforcement points are unchanged: one precedes sampling and one applies returned limits.

summary: A stored thumbnail format mismatch leaves the discarded WebGPU canvas configured.
evidence: load sizes and configures the canvas before checking the actual format against the cached format. On mismatch it returns null, and makeCell detaches that canvas and replaces it without releasing its backing; its abort callback now owns only the replacement.
felt_impact: Avoids transient graphics memory retention when the stored format cannot be presented.
proposed_fix: Unconfigure and zero the rejected canvas before returning the existing cache miss.
check: Mock a stored format mismatch and verify no upload and immediate release; verify exact cached upload and Grade handoff separately.
notes: 17 targeted thumbnail and publication Node tests pass. Real-app stored-thumbnail smoke still needed.

summary: Cancelling a native Library upload leaves its abort listener on the owner and can start a fresh worker solely to cancel a dead stream.
evidence: sendStreamed invokes cancel on a failure. Unlike end, cancel skipped listener removal and called ensureWorker even after failWorker had cleared and terminated the worker. A mocked worker crash reproduces both.
proposed_fix: Detach the listener on cancel and send a cancel message only to an existing worker.
check: Simulate a worker crash and assert that explicit stream cancellation detaches the listener without creating a worker.
notes: Six targeted upload and detail-stream Node tests pass. Native detail cancellation is an additional real-app smoke, beyond the standard quick Library check.

summary: Releasing a ready picture underreports retained thumbnail GPU memory.
evidence: The release POST replaced the same ready client entry with ready bytes alone, while other reports include the detached tile pool. When ready bytes reach zero the poll skips them entirely. A Node reproduction reports 0 despite a still-owned 1,024-byte tile.
felt_impact: Shared admission can briefly count pooled surfaces as free memory. No real-device timing measured.
proposed_fix: Include tile-pool bytes in the existing release report, without changing capacity or eviction.
check: library-single-ready.test.js and library-gpu-residency.test.js passed (16). Real app: move Grid to Single and back with pooled tiles present.

summary: A delayed native-detail heartbeat can recreate a released GPU reservation.
evidence: Navigation destroys native planes and DELETEs the raw-budget UUID, but an overlapping renewal POST upserts the same UUID in gpu_delivery.py. With no live owner left to clean it up, the backend can retain it until the existing 30-second expiry. A Node simulation processed DELETE before POST and reproduced the orphan.
felt_impact: Phantom GPU usage can delay other work until the existing lease expires.
proposed_fix: Keep the immediate release and repeat it after any still-in-flight renewal settles. Keep the same cadence, size and expiry.
check: library-gpu-raw.test.js and library-invalid-gpu-retry.test.js passed (43). Real app: request native detail and leave while the lease is active.

summary: A thumbnail plan invalidated while waiting for navigation can still start source admission and CPU fallback.
evidence: The generation was checked when the plan returned and again after development, but not when beforeSource resumed. The invalidation cannot cancel a job that has not been submitted. A delayed navigation test against the GPU-oversize path observed both source and CPU asks even though the old result was discarded.
felt_impact: Stale work can consume a source lane and memory while the current thumbnails wait. No real-app timing measured.
proposed_fix: Recheck the plan generation before promoting or submitting development.
check: library-scenes.test.js, library-scene-scheduler.test.js and library-grants.test.js passed (112). Real app: change a grade during navigation and exercise the repaired oversize thumbnail.

summary: An unfinished stored thumbnail can publish the previous HDR/SDR rendition after an HDR toggle.
evidence: toggleHDR does not remove a visible cell that has not populated meta yet. Its in-flight stored upload checks cell ownership but not displayEpoch. On completion makeCell publishes old-lane pixels and stamps them with the new display epoch. A Node reproduction held the SDR request through the toggle and saw SDR publish instead of HDR.
felt_impact: A tile can visibly disagree with the active rendition until the next redraw.
proposed_fix: Reject the obsolete display epoch and retry the current rendition on a fresh canvas before publishing.
check: library-publication.test.js passed (9) with the patch applied only to scratch. Real app: toggle HDR during a cold stored-thumbnail load.
notes: Patch is recorded only. No pixel-changing code was applied to the sprint branch.

summary: The hidden delivery renderer starts more permit requests while a previous heartbeat is unresolved.
evidence: Four fake one-second ticks against a delayed fetch started four unresolved GETs. The endpoint touches the delivery heartbeat and takes the shared broker lock for accounting; heartbeat freshness is used by export and Proof to choose GPU delivery.
felt_impact: Extra queued work during a backend stall. Normal-operation responsiveness was not measured.
proposed_fix: Use a single-flight heartbeat, checking that delivery still recovers and falls back correctly under a slow or stalled backend.
check: Targeted Node delayed-fetch simulation confirmed the overlap. Export and Proof coverage is needed before fixing.

summary: A ready-surface poll can issue two broker requests every 100 ms while a GPU-backed ready picture is retained.
evidence: The timer has a single-flight guard. Each eligible tick still does a permit GET followed by a readyMemory activity POST, and both run shared accounting under the broker lock. Ten simulated eligible ticks produced 20 requests. They also use different snapshots.
felt_impact: Up to about 20 steady-state requests per eligible window per second, without a measured effect on time to picture.
proposed_fix: Coordinate a single broker snapshot with the backend owner, preserving the existing yield rules, expiry and cadence.
check: Targeted Node request-count simulation confirmed no poll overlap and counted both requests. Verify retained pictures still yield to Grade and delivery in the app.
notes: The recon canvas width and height reads are backing-store dimensions, not forced DOM layout. No layout-loop finding was inferred from those reads.

summary: The Desktop pressure relay and Library HTTP reports can overwrite each other with stale cache caps.
evidence: R2-3 orders HTTP reports only. The Desktop relays GET /memory, which can return a previously completed snapshot, and apply() replaces the same limits as POST /memory-report. A delayed HTTP simulation replaced a newly relayed 200-byte cap with the older 400-byte cap. The reverse delivery order can also overwrite a fresh report. sampleId identifies the process census, not the age of the dynamic cache caps.
felt_impact: An old low cap can evict too much, or an old high cap can briefly allow excess residency.
proposed_fix: Give the cap snapshot an ordering shared by both channels, or choose a single cap authority. Keep pressure-triggered reclaim independent and retain all approved limits.
check: Targeted Node delayed-response simulation confirmed unordered application. Add an end-to-end ordering test for both transports before changing ownership.
notes: A reliable ordering or single-authority contract spans backend and Desktop, outside this review package.

felt_impact: Small on the CPU fallback only, commonly below 1 ms, potentially a few ms for long brush histories. No GPU slider change; magnitude is unmeasured.
summary: The JPEG CPU preview serializes and parses the local draft immediately before serializing it again in the HTTP body.
evidence: localAdjustments returns plain session JSON plus plain editor data, and no await occurs before the outer JSON.stringify; raw CPU preview already sends the draft directly.
proposed_fix: Keep the outer synchronous request serialization and omit the inner JSON round trip.
check: denoise-preview-presentation.test.js verifies nested draft values, bypass, and comparison cache priority.

felt_impact: Likely below 1 ms per avoided clone with ordinary settings and no change to the backend wait. Relevant only while a non-neutral geometry map is missing or in flight.
summary: The geometry-map path clones the full adjustment tree even when it joins an existing request or is in backoff.
evidence: withCapacityBackoff invokes the fetch callback synchronously or declines without invoking it; request JSON in that callback is a complete snapshot before fetch starts.
proposed_fix: Serialize the adjustment object in the existing fetch callback, once only when sending.
check: geometry-math.test.js verifies the body, same-edit sharing, newer revision independence and capacity recovery.

felt_impact: Near zero with small masks. Long brush histories may save a few ms of main-thread work per overlay frame with mapped geometry, mainly while painting; not measured and no rendering speedup claimed.
summary: Brush overlay frames project every committed point even with a hidden, authoritative or cached mask, and fallback replay repeatedly reacquires the erase context.
evidence: Overlay callers share a keyed raster cache, but point projection preceded visibility and cache checks. The erase canvas retains one 2D context throughout ordered paint/erase replay. The focused test reproduced unnecessary work and checks the resulting alpha and replay order.
proposed_fix: Project stored strokes on fallback raster misses only, and retain the erase context for replay and readback.
check: mask-sampling.test.js checks hidden/authoritative paths, ordered replay, fallback alpha and reuse; real Grade mask overlay check recommended.

summary: A failed Retouch cancel notification leaves an unhandled fetch rejection.
evidence: The click sets the local cancellation flag, then starts a fire-and-forget POST with no rejection handler. The flag still blocks unstarted commands when the backend is unreachable.
proposed_fix: Consume and log the network failure without creating a new user message or changing the local cancel.
check: retouch-source-refresh.test.js clicks Cancel with a rejected fetch and checks the local flag and exact request.

notes: Patch covers edits or drafts present before issuing the load, not the separate window while the server is opening the replacement. Verify with a real sidecar change during a Grade edit before landing.
summary: A clean sidecar check can replace a newer local edit with an external grade.
evidence: A held check is sent with unsaved=false. A slider moves before its reload response arrives. tick loads the external grade anyway, activates a replacement session, and clears documentDirty. The regression reproduced the external session activation before the fix.
proposed_fix: Before automatically loading, verify the same photo and edit token are still clean after draining the already queued edit; let the next poll detect the conflict normally.
check: grade-background-pause.test.js holds the check response, edits locally, verifies the next check reports unsaved, and proves a later clean reload still works.

notes: Only extends the guard to Retouch, which leaves the global adjustment tree unchanged. Other commands can intentionally alter it and need separate merge semantics.
summary: Finishing a Retouch repair can discard a global slider edit made while the repair is in flight.
evidence: set_repairs sends a whole-document acknowledgement but has no global generation guard. A delayed source refresh allowed Exposure to change to 0.7 before the old acknowledgement reset it to 0. The next global save would send the reset value.
proposed_fix: Capture the global edit generation for set_repairs, compare it after source refresh, and preserve newer optimistic adjustments while accepting the repair.
check: edit-sync-retry.test.js delays repair source refresh and checks both the acknowledged repair and the next exact global adjustment payload; exercise on a real long repair.

felt_impact: Likely up to a few ms less main-thread work in a burst with fine or snap held; no expected render-compute change and impact unmeasured.
notes: Visible readout and hover correction are why the code is not landed. Check Ctrl/Shift in the real app, including labels on Temperature.
summary: Hovered modifier sliders rebuild their tick markup per input, and queued work can reapply fine mode after pointer leave.
evidence: Two inputs before a frame queued two callbacks, rebuilt all 41 fine ticks twice, and reformatted the same value from 0.48 to 0.480. The same callback applies cached modifiers without checking the current hover. Snap mode also measures overlap for each rebuilt label.
proposed_fix: Invalidate the ordinary readout on each input, process only the latest input once per frame, and check the hover again before decorating.
check: control-panel-values.test.js checks final fine readout, one tick build, and ordinary styling after leaving before the frame.

felt_impact: Small main-thread improvement, likely below 1 ms per ordinary input. No change to CPU/GPU render wait; not measured.
summary: The save status chrome replaces unchanged text nodes on every global edit and twice per successful idle poll.
evidence: markGlobalEditDirty calls syncProjectBadge per input, which calls render. That function assigned the same photo title, autosave label and save state even after the first dirty transition. The backend returns a full session only when its current same-photo session ID was replaced, not for unchanged polls.
proposed_fix: Set text only when it changed. Keep processing each edit token, the save delay and all original UI states.
check: grade-background-pause.test.js verifies title, dirty status and repeated edit notifications without unchanged text writes; grade-open-loading also passes.

summary: A truncated candidate response rejects the detached SDR Match worker.
evidence: The Match request launches the worker with void; response.json was outside both fetch catch blocks. The backend already has a deadline and CPU fallback for a candidate never returned.
proposed_fix: Log the candidate decode error and end the worker; leave the backend fallback and visible status alone.
check: sdr-match-session.test.js checks that a rejected candidate decode neither rejects the worker nor submits GPU work.

felt_impact: Likely sub-millisecond less main-thread work per input, with fewer DOM mutations during fast drags. No render-compute change; unmeasured.
summary: Every ordinary Grade input recreates the Film stock fact chips even when the stock facts have not changed.
evidence: Normal range input calls commitAdjustmentValue, then renderControlState, renderFilmStockControls and renderFilmPanel. renderFilmPanel unconditionally replaced the two or four chip spans, even for another module or a Look Strength edit.
proposed_fix: Replace the chip spans only when the fact count or displayed text differs.
check: film-presets.test.js checks chip identity on strength change and regenerated facts after a stock change.

felt_impact: Avoids many text and accessibility mutations per input; estimate under a few ms of main-thread time on a busy drag. No change to render computation; unmeasured.
summary: Editing one global slider rewrites the text and accessible value for all non-editing Grade readouts.
evidence: Normal input calls commitAdjustmentValue, which refreshes all value outputs; each assignment replaced a text node or attribute even when unchanged. On a Film control this can run twice through syncControlsFromState.
proposed_fix: Only assign different text and ARIA values, while syncing controls whose ARIA value is missing and protecting active typed input.
check: control-panel-values.test.js checks changed and unchanged displayed/accessible values, a replacement control, and a readout being typed.

felt_impact: No material normal slider wait change expected. Avoids five idle wake-ups per second in this fallback state and helps tests that wait for the view to become idle.
notes: Do not remove the fallback timer on ordinary in-flight interactions; existing wakeups must still prove they cover exact recovery before changing scheduling.
summary: A queued exact highlight anchor keeps waking every 200 ms after Grade settles on a reduced picture.
evidence: A fake timer starting with a current reduced, non-exact presentation rearmed 20 times with no measurement and still had a scheduled callback. The dispatch has no terminal-preview guard; only changing photo/lane or reaching an exact accepted frame escapes that branch.
proposed_fix: When no exact frame is possible, park the pending anchor without polling and wake it on a new exact presentation or relevant recovery event.
check: Extend native-anchor-scheduling.test.js for terminal refusal, recovery and interaction fencing, then check bounded peak on a real reduced-to-exact recovery.

felt_impact: Other API calls could wait for the entire remaining copy and decode. The upload itself is not expected to complete faster.
notes: The browser frontend already serializes byte uploads. The normal desktop path uses import jobs.
summary: A browser upload blocks the shared API loop while writing and decoding the photo.
evidence: The async FastAPI handler called the synchronous file write and SessionStore.create_session directly. A held decoder prevented a concurrent /health request from making progress on the old code.
proposed_fix: Make this a synchronous FastAPI worker route, preserving temp-file ownership, exact bytes and decoder behavior.
check: test_api.py: concurrent health request, upload success/failure, real PNG preview/scopes and eject cleanup.

summary: A failed encode leaves partial scratch files in the RAW thumbnail and overlay caches.
evidence: The cleanup finally followed rather than enclosed np.savez_compressed in this writer and OverlayMaps.build (library_overlays.py:368). Injecting a short disk write left a .tmp file in both cache directories.
proposed_fix: Put temp creation, encoding, close and publication under the existing cleanup finally.
check: test_library_cache.py: simulate a partial write in both cache writers and verify no scratch file remains.

notes: After approval verify Denoise on a real RAW across re-development and the normal GPU preview.
summary: RAW re-development can reuse the previous source's Denoise model under the same session ID.
evidence: The old cache's epoch advances at import start, but replacement creates a fresh cache starting at zero. The Grade model key is session ID and epoch. The HTTP regression returns the cached old sample 0.02328498475253582 instead of the new source's 0.0.
proposed_fix: Advance the new cache's epoch past the old live epoch before publishing the replacement.
check: test_denoise_native_model.py: Grade endpoint refits after same-session development and developed source pixels are unchanged by the epoch change. Existing RAW cleanup undo/redo tests also pass.

felt_impact: Avoids a transient float32 image, up to 315 MB for the existing 5120 px square reduction limit (about 210 MB for 3:2). Releases the uint8 input early. Whole Library wait unmeasured. On a 5120×3414 RGB NumPy fixture the stage medians were 21.0 ms before and 21.3 ms after across five runs, indistinguishable at the proposed 10% threshold. This is a memory win, not a measured speed win.
notes: For stage-only NumPy timing, differences under 10% count as noise due to allocator and shared-machine variability.
summary: Reduced Library PNG loading allocates a second full float32 sample frame for a scalar multiply.
evidence: The RGB uint8 samples were converted to float32 and then multiplied out-of-place before the in-place color transform. The exact old intermediate and both final source renditions match the in-place multiply.
proposed_fix: Convert once, release the reduced uint8 input, and multiply the owned float buffer in place.
check: test_library_reduced.py: all 256 byte codes match the old normalization and both source renditions match bit for bit.

summary: The Library detail upload limit is checked only after buffering the entire body when no length is declared.
evidence: The real endpoint consumed all 35 supplied 1 MiB chunks even after passing its existing 32 MiB limit, before rejecting. Upload owner validation runs later in LibraryPictureCache.upload_native.
proposed_fix: Apply the same byte limit before appending each chunk, preserving the accepted bytes and rejection status/detail.
check: test_library_gpu_raw.py: no-read-past-limit ASGI upload and accepted streamed byte equality.

summary: Failed Library settings or file-command journal flushes leave temp files behind.
evidence: Both Library atomic_json and library_file_io.durable start cleanup after the temporary file closes. Injected fsync failure left a .tmp in each case while preserving the original destination.
proposed_fix: Enclose the writes and fsync in the cleanup finally without changing publication or serialized bytes.
check: test_library_membership.py failure injections and test_library_file_commands.py rename/move recovery boundaries.

summary: RAW re-development can install pixels decoded with obsolete source interpretation or reference white.
evidence: ImportJobManager snapshots the source interpretation and reference white before decode. The replacement checks only fingerprint, then copies the live interpretation and white onto the candidate. Tests advance either setting while the old candidate is pending and show it is still accepted. Display P3 interpretation produces a different pixel array.
proposed_fix: Reject the candidate through the existing RAW re-development mismatch path if either decode input has changed.
check: test_extended_formats.py: both context changes preserve the active object, revision and exact pixels, plus two normal re-development cases.

summary: A session opened during the first source-mip initialization can permanently miss the shared store.
evidence: The resolved flag became true before creating the root and store. Pausing mkdir let a second concurrent session return None, which LoadedSession otherwise keeps for its lifetime.
proposed_fix: Serialize first initialization and publish the resolved flag only after the result is ready.

evidence: ensureIntermediate creates finishTexture but resetSession destroys a hand-written list that lacks it before clearing the map and replacing scope/presentation references. A fake device showed baseTexture destroyed and finishTexture undestroyed. One retired RGBA16F texture is 8 bytes per pixel per canvas, or 11.5 MB at 1600×900, until GC/device cleanup.

proposed_fix: Use the existing destroyIntermediate helper in the current deferred-destroy callback rather than maintaining a second ownership list.

notes: Shared with gpu-delivery.js resets, so left for coordinated verification.

summary: Every foreground Grade render waits on delivery-accounting IPC even when no GPU reservation is held.
evidence: initialize starts a 100 ms POST heartbeat and sets deliveryActivityTimer; renderToFrame and renderTiledTo await another POST before source/cache work. reportDeliveryActivity first builds a resource snapshot. Backend gpu_delivery.py::activity recalculates scheduler/RAW/delivery activity even on an idle reply. If a reservation remains, Grade polls at 20 ms with no render cancellation or deadline.
felt_impact: Broadest candidate. Removing the idle gate could shave one request/JSON/accounting round trip from warm Exposure/Contrast and Denoise on/off on both scales. Cold Grain is less likely to benefit materially. Idle milliseconds unmeasured. Under contention the obsolete wait can delay the newest frame until release. Audit baseline Tone probes and warm toggle_on/off at Fit and 100%; instrument from budget wait start to first fenced frame, and add a separate competing delivery/RAW run.
proposed_fix: Measure first. Move per-frame work to a cancellable session-scoped admission protocol that can safely reuse explicit no-contention knowledge. Keep the current budget, expiry, preemption and contention safety, with one owner for heartbeat and foreground reporting.
check: Count POSTs and release wait with a stub, then compare the same-machine baseline and one simultaneous delivery safety check.
notes: Do not change the budget or replace the authoritative reservation check with a TTL guess.

summary: Tiled drag frames run an exact peak reduction and wait for its readback even when the draft peak is not published.
evidence: The non-noise tiled encoder builds a 64×64 peak grid and scans finished pixels in every tile, copies the result, then awaits mapAsync. It suppresses exactScopePeak publication for grainIdentity only after paying both costs. Apps await the renderer before recording an accepted frame. Normal settled scopes have a separate measured/current path.
felt_impact: Likely best 100% candidate on large tiled, Film or Denoise frames; a real pass over all processed tile pixels plus a small map/fence. Potentially visible on Exposure/Contrast and warm Denoise toggles when tiled. None on ordinary Direct Fit. Magnitude unmeasured. Large at 100% baseline and Film/Detail/Denoise Tone probes plus toggle_on/off; compare real submit, first fenced frame and settle against reduction/readback stages.
proposed_fix: Measure reduction time and publication consumers. For Grade only, avoid measuring discarded draft peaks and investigate handing current published peaks off without holding presentation; keep the same exact settled/measurement/Proof result.
check: Use separate reduction and map attribution in the audit, then scope-peak-toggle-interaction.js and tiled/direct parity plus a same-machine 100% before/after.

summary: Packed Detail bands and the tiled Clarity map do not fully identify the input picture they were built from.
evidence: Curve shape is uploaded to a separate curve buffer and can change without changing packed parameters or the source proxy identity. Packed Global and Local Detail keys omit those curve samples and the Denoise reconstruction identity; Clarity names Denoise controls but also omits global curve shape. When identical halo neighbors are resident, assemblePackedHalo reuses the old textures under the same key, after the base pass has already drawn different pixels. Lens-side and pan identity checks do not protect this separate cache.
felt_impact: Correctness, not a speed win. Where the halo happens to match, a warm Denoise toggle can look fast because it reads stale bands. Ordinary Tone Exposure/Contrast already changes the key. Compare Curves own steps and Denoise toggle_on/off with Detail ON at 100% against a cold-cache or Direct reference.
proposed_fix: Include the Grade frame's curve signatures, source epoch and actual reconstruction identity in the applicable Detail inputs. Keep Global bands independent of Local curve changes.
check: Apply patch, then a tiled warm Curve-shape/Denoise toggle with matching halo and warmed neighbors against forced cache-cold execution; run tiled-cpu-detail-parity.js.
notes: Patch applies to Grade only. Syntax checked; pixels not verified without GPU.

summary: A cancelled or failed tile encoder can leave an unwritten Detail band cached as a hit.
evidence: detailBandTile registers a texture immediately, then the encoder records the copy. Cancellation before a four-tile batch is submitted discards the commands. The finally block evicts unsubmitted Denoise entries, not Detail entries; the next same-input pass can assemble its halo from those textures as if they were written. The visible frame can then consume empty band data at a reused tile.
felt_impact: Picture correctness. A cancelled zoom, pan or superseded tiled frame can produce incorrect Detail on a later reuse. At 100% quick Denoise or Tone changes are a stress case, but stock audit may settle between samples and miss the interleaving.
proposed_fix: Track new band allocations within the encoder, forget ones in abandoned batches, and discard new bands from passes rejected by GPU validation. Keep caches from successful submitted batches.
check: Failure injection with cancellation after one Detail tile but before a batch submit, then a same-key rerender; tiled-cpu-detail-parity.js and performance/roi-pan-cache.js after approval.
notes: Patch scoped to Grade, applies with R5-6, syntax checked. No GPU reproduction run.

summary: Grade device rebuild keeps GPU peak resources from the lost device.

A fake old/new device reproduced the original reuse, and the isolated patch rebuilt the cache, destroyed both target resources and ignored a late old-device compile.

proposed_fix: Retire the old peak pool and shader/pipeline cache on Grade rebuild; gate asynchronous compilation publication on the originating GPU device.
check: Extend device-loss-fallback.js to prime tiled peak and the compute reduction before loss, then exercise both on the replacement device.
notes: Grade rebuild is called only from app-boot. The patch changes failure-path preview recovery, not the intended picture.

summary: Output-stage controls invalidate earlier Detail caches that never read those controls.
evidence: detailBandIdentity serializes nearly the entire packed grade, while the packed bands come from the base or local candidate before Film finish, vignette and output exposure. For example VIGNETTE_AMOUNT only appears in the finish shader and not in the base or Detail passes, but changing it changes the global band key and local preceding identity. Same-size/tile-layout draws pay two band passes again. Frame Clarity excludes only some Film slots.
felt_impact: Likely no direct Exposure/Contrast or Denoise toggle gain because those really change Detail's input. Could improve large tiled output-stage drags with Detail already active. Audit own Film grain or Vignette drag with Detail also ON at 100%; the stock single-module rows will not isolate this interaction.
proposed_fix: After fixing R5-6, separate base/local input fingerprints from post-Detail output controls. Keep real base-stage Film dependencies and each local's upstream inputs; do not change trim allowances.
check: Prove cache hits on a post-Detail-only edit and output parity vs cold cache, then run a paired 100% combo timing.

summary: A live scope can get ahead of the next already pending drag frame on the GPU.
evidence: Frame completion clears frameInFlight, starts a matching deferred interactive scope, and only then requests the pending drag frame. runGpuScopeRequest can immediately submit analyzeScope, which only checks that a frame is not currently in flight, and GPU work is FIFO. If a newer edit wins during map, request-level currentness is checked only after unpack. Existing 100 ms throttling means this is not a readback for every input.
felt_impact: Potential intermittent Fit Exposure/Contrast pacing benefit under sustained input, not all frames and likely no first-feedback improvement. A discrete warm Denoise toggle should see little or none unless it lands behind a live scope. Tiled interactive scopes are already skipped. Check gaps between fenced frames during the baseline/Film Fit Tone probes; existing first/settle alone may miss it.
proposed_fix: Compare explicit frame-first admission for the pending scope, and reject stale scope results before unpacking, without changing the settled readout or removing live scopes.
check: Deterministic scheduler scope/frame-order test plus same-machine Fit audit with scope timing and current frame intervals.

summary: Staging cleanup can fence the wrong device or miss destruction during a rebuild.
evidence: copyChunkStaged creates staging buffers on renderer.device, yields in mapAsync, then reads the mutable renderer.device again for the encoder and submission. releaseStaging clears its arrays and then reads renderer.device.queue, which can be null or replaced after Grade rebuild. A null device throws before buffer destroy; a new device fences unrelated work. Streaming/strip/region transport all use the shared helper. A fake replacement-device check confirmed that null loses the only staging reference without a destroy and a new queue is fenced instead of the old queue.
felt_impact: No expected steady-state Exposure/Contrast or warm Denoise effect. Cold Fit/large 100% source upload during device loss can fail twice and delay recovery. The audit has cold Denoise steps but only a forced loss during upload isolates it.
proposed_fix: Capture the owning device for a transfer and its staging ring, use only that queue, and guarantee buffer destruction in finally without publishing a retired source. Qualify delivery uses before landing.
check: Fake device switch while awaiting map or body read, followed by source-transport.test.js and the covering device-loss, large source and delivery checks.
notes: Open ownership repair. R5-1 protects the pan cache publication race, not this shared device/staging boundary.
